pages.title: C++ code syntax and extensions
pages.description: C++ code syntax and extensions for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
Link CyUI::Code (C++17) for the catalogue, lexer service and read-only views; CyUI::CodeEditor (C++20) adds the common editable widget. Core-only builds do not compile or link any lexer. CMake resolves dependencies automatically and exports CYUI_CODE_LANGUAGE_CATALOGUE=1. No network fetch or Python is needed to build the committed catalogue. Exactly one compatible ImGui instance is used.

Built-in modes#

codeLanguages() returns 102 owned metadata snapshots. The canonical list, file associations and original shader profiles are in data/code-languages.json. It covers the Notepad++ syntax-mode list used by the host migration, plus HLSL, GLSL, Markdown, TSX and an Unreal C++ profile. Each mode has its own fixture. NFO intentionally displays as plain text: decoding OEM code pages belongs to the host. Internal Search uses a diagnostic-list lexer; it is not a search engine. Shared engines do not include Notepad++'s UI, plugin ABI or configuration format.

codeLanguageFromName(idOrName) accepts catalogue IDs/display names and a few aliases; unknown names return plain. codeLanguageForPath(path) checks exact filenames, then case-insensitive extensions. A host may add project context (Unreal headers are ambiguous without it) or let the user select a mode manually. Plugin associations take precedence; removing a definition restores built-ins. Ambiguous associations between plugins are deterministic by stable numeric ID.

Add a syntax from an application plugin#

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/Code.h>cyui::CodeLanguageDefinition syntax;syntax.id = "my-plugin/config";  // stable, namespaced IDsyntax.name = "My configuration";syntax.extensions = {"mycfg"}; // no leading dotcyui::CodeSyntaxRules rules;rules.keywords = {"option", "section"};rules.types = {"number", "vector"};rules.lineComment = "#";rules.blockCommentStart = "/*";rules.blockCommentEnd = "*/";syntax.rules = rules;const auto language = cyui::registerCodeLanguage(syntax);// view.setText(source, language, documentRevision);// editor.setLanguage(language);// On plugin removal, after stopping calls and before unloading its code:cyui::unregisterCodeLanguage(syntax.id);

Alternatively set base to a built-in language and wordLists (0-based Lexilla sets) and optional lexer properties. Empty word-list entries inherit the base. Rules support one line-comment delimiter, one block pair, quote characters, escaping and case-sensitive/insensitive word sets. They are deliberately simpler than a grammar. For nested constructs, embedded languages or a custom parser, provide highlight(std::string_view) -> std::vector<CodeToken> instead. Callback results take precedence over rules; rules take precedence over the base engine.

Tokens use raw UTF-8 byte offsets, never display columns, UTF-16 positions or tab expansion. Ranges must be nonempty, sorted, nonoverlapping, within the snapshot, and start/end on code-point boundaries. Gaps remain neutral. Unknown roles and invalid spans throw before replacing a prepared CodeDocument. Themes map roles through palette colors; plugins do not supply literal UI colors. Bounds apply to definition sizes and 32 MiB source snapshots. Trusted plugin code still needs host error handling and time limits where its architecture permits them.

Registration updates an existing plugin ID without changing its numeric value. Built-in values 0..13 are preserved; dynamic values use the high bit. Do not persist dynamic numbers: persist the string ID. Built-in IDs cannot be replaced; hash collisions are rejected. Registry snapshots are synchronized, and callbacks run outside its mutex. Callback capture/library lifetime belongs to the host; unregister does not wait for already running callbacks. Stop/join those calls before unloading a library or destroying captured services.

Caching, editing and limits#

CodeDocument caches document and registry revisions. CodeEditor refreshes syntax only when the native text revision or registry changes. Lexilla currently lexes the complete bounded snapshot after an edit; this is not an incremental parser. A glyph edit made during rendering receives updated shared colors on the next frame. refreshSyntax() prepares explicitly, including in headless tests. Syntax preparation never changes text bytes, cursor state or Undo history. setSyntaxEnabled(false) lets hosts retain richer existing lexical/semantic adapters on the same native editor without a second widget implementation.

This is lexical coloring, not language-server completion, refactoring or compiler semantics. Legacy Python modules keep their existing implementation; the new native registry/callback API described here is C++ only. A Python native binding is not supplied by this change.

Bundled dependencies#

The exact Lexilla, Scintilla-header and SciTE-property revisions and archive hashes are recorded in third_party/code-syntax.lock.json. The committed catalogue requires no network or Python to build. Only the selected Lexilla engines and support library compile; the Scintilla editing UI is excluded. Retain all three licenses and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Log files#

CodeLanguage::log is selected automatically for .log / .logs files. It colors the complete line using semantic palette roles, with normal INFO and untagged lines left in the default text color:

Level word (case-insensitive) Role / default appearance
Error, Fatal, Critical, Panic, Exception error / red
Warning, Warn warning / orange
Debug, Trace, Verbose, VeryVerbose comment / subdued
Everything else, including Info text / normal

Matching uses complete words, so ErrorCode, WarningCount and traceback are not severity markers. Error takes priority over Warning, then debug verbosity. This supports bracketed levels, Unreal LogTemp: Error:, JSON level fields and common timestamp/category prefixes. ANSI CSI sequences are skipped when detecting level words; source bytes remain intact. Wrapped visual rows inherit the same color. Stack-trace continuation lines without a level remain normal; inferred multiline events and stripping escape sequences belong to a dedicated log-viewing host. Plugins can inherit base = CodeLanguage::log for other extensions, or supply a callback for a logger with different level names or classification rules.

Verse#

CodeLanguage::verse / verse selects the original native Verse scanner; .verse matching is case-insensitive, including *.digest.verse. No UEFN SDK, new Lexilla engine or language server is linked. CodeEditor and CodeDocument use the same tokens. Keywords, built-in types, effect/access specifiers, attributes, call names, decimal/hexadecimal/exponent numbers, strings and characters have semantic palette roles. # comments, nested <# ... #> comments and <#> indented comments preserve their state across lines. Double-quoted interpolation colors expressions, including nested braces, strings and comments; escaped braces stay string text. Unterminated comments/strings remain colored through EOF. Interpolation/string nesting is bounded to 63 frames; a deeper remainder is displayed as string text. Syntax preparation never edits source or Undo history.

Plugins can inherit base = CodeLanguage::verse; word sets 0/1/2 replace keyword, type and function families. Empty entries inherit defaults. Rules/callbacks still take precedence; associations still restore after plugin removal. This is lexical support, not Verse compilation, UEFN completion or semantic analysis.

References: Book of Verse and Epic's Verse reference.

pages.title: Themes, layout and migration
pages.description: Themes, layout and migration for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
1. Never hard-code a colour. Take every colour from cyui::palette(), by its role:

    • bg0 is the deepest ground: canvases, timelines, wells, the status bar.
    • bg1 is the panel ground.
    • bg2 is for headers, cards and popups.
    • bg3 is for fields and buttons at rest; bg4 when hovered; bg5 when pressed or active.
    • line and lineStrong are for lines.
    • text, textDim and textFaint are the three text levels.
    • accent, accentHover, accentDim, accentText and selection: there is one accent, used only for what is active, selected or the main action.
    • success, warning, error and info carry meaning.

    For a variant, use cyui::alpha / mix / brighter / darker. For series of things (tracks, layers, tags), use cyui::categorical(i).

  2. Never hard-code a size in pixels. Wrap it: cyui::dp(12.0f), cyui::dp(8, 4). Prefer sizes derived from the style: ImGui::GetFrameHeight(), ImGui::GetFontSize(), ImGui::GetStyle()....

  3. Text hierarchy.

    • cyui::heading(t, 1|2|3) for titles.
    • cyui::sectionTitle for groups in a panel.
    • cyui::overline("UPPERCASE") for compact uppercase labels.
    • cyui::textDim for labels and secondary info.
    • cyui::textFaint for hints.

    Do not make titles with ImGui::Text plus a colour push.

  4. One primary button per view. Use cyui::primaryButton for the main action, cyui::button (secondary) for the rest, cyui::ghostButton or cyui::iconButton in toolbars, and cyui::dangerButton for destructive actions.

  5. Toolbars are icon buttons. Use cyui::iconButton(icon::x, "Tooltip (Shortcut)", active). Separate groups with cyui::toolbarSeparator(). Every icon button must have a tooltip that names the action and its shortcut.

  6. Settings and inspectors are property tables (beginProperties / property / endProperties), inside collapsible sections (beginSection). Do not use free-floating ImGui::Text("Label:"); ImGui::SameLine(); ImGui::SliderFloat(...) lines.

  7. Group related content in cards (beginCard / endCard). Use toned cards (Tone::accent / warning / error) only to draw attention.

  8. Empty panels say why. Use cyui::emptyState("No layers yet", "Drop an image or press Ctrl+N", icon::photo). Never leave a blank panel.

  9. Feedback is visible.

    • cyui::notify("Saved", Tone::success) for events.
    • cyui::callout(Tone::warning, ...) for standing conditions.
    • progressBar / spinner for work in progress.
    • badge and statusDot for state.

  10. Tooltips are delayed and wrapped. Use cyui::tooltip(text) after an item. Use cyui::helpMarker(text) to explain an option.

  11. Keep stock ImGui wherever it already reads well: Checkbox, InputText, ColorEdit, tables, trees, menus, tab bars, DragFloat2. The theme styles them. Do not wrap or reinvent them.

  12. Prefer the RAII helpers ScopedColor, ScopedVar, ScopedFont, ScopedID and ScopedDisabled over manual Push/Pop pairs.

Migrate an ImGui interface#

Work panel by panel. Change the look, not the behaviour. Keep IDs, labels and logic as they are.

Stock / old code CyUI
ImGui::StyleColorsDark(); style.Colors[...] = ... (theme function) delete it; cyui::apply(config); cyui::loadFonts();
IM_COL32(40,42,50,255) or ImVec4(...) literals in drawing code cyui::palette().bg3 (pick by role)
10.0f pixel literals in custom drawing cyui::dp(10.0f)
ImGui::Button("OK") main action of a dialog/panel cyui::primaryButton("OK")
ImGui::Button("Delete") cyui::dangerButton("Delete")
ImGui::Button("X") / ImGui::SmallButton in toolbars cyui::iconButton(cyui::icon::close, "Close")
ImGui::Button(icon) + if (selected) PushStyleColor(...) tool buttons cyui::iconButton(icon, tip, selected)
ImGui::Checkbox for an on/off setting cyui::toggleSwitch("Label", &v) (keep Checkbox in lists/tables)
row of RadioButtons / buttons for a mode cyui::segmented("##mode", labels, n, &mode)
ImGui::Text("Section"); ImGui::Separator(); cyui::sectionTitle("Section") or cyui::beginSection("Section")
ImGui::TextColored(gray, ...) cyui::textDim(...) / cyui::textFaint(...)
ImGui::Text("Name:"); SameLine(); InputText(...) stacks beginProperties + property("Name") + the widget
ImGui::SliderFloat in an inspector cyui::sliderBar(id, &v, min, max, "%.2f", -1) (or keep SliderFloat)
ImGui::InputText used as a filter cyui::searchField("##filter", buf, size, "Search")
ImGui::BeginChild(..., true) used as a box cyui::beginCard(id, "Title") ... cyui::endCard()
ImGui::ProgressBar cyui::progressBar(f, size, overlay, tone)
ImGui::OpenPopup + BeginPopupModal confirm dialog cyui::beginModal + cyui::modalButtons
status messages printed in a panel cyui::notify(...)
custom main-window bars with SetNextWindowPos hacks cyui::beginTopBar / beginStatusBar / beginSidebar
audio knobs / faders / meters drawn by hand cyui::knob / cyui::fader / cyui::meter

Custom-drawn views (canvases, node editors, timelines, curves) keep their drawing code. Swap their colour constants for palette roles:

  • grounds: bg0
  • grid: grid / gridStrong
  • selection: selection plus an accent outline
  • text: text / textDim
  • handles: bg5, or accent when active

Check your work: open cyui::showGallery() from a debug menu, switch themes and densities, and look at the app in all five themes. Nothing may stay dark-on-dark or light-on-light.

pages.title: Native Diff viewer
pages.description: Native Diff viewer for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
Select Diff in CYUI_MODULES, include <cyui/modules/Diff.h> and link CyUI::Diff. The module depends on Core and Code, with the host's existing ImGui instance; it adds no platform backend, Git integration or editor implementation.

Prepare a DiffDocument with setTexts or setUnified, then retain a DiffState per view and call diffViewer(id, state, document, size). Its API and state/result layout remain compatible with earlier versions. Source preparation stays in the document; repeatedly drawing a prepared view does not recompute the diff.

Both split columns are now painted inside one child canvas, using exactly the same visible row origin. Wheel/trackpad input over either column and the common vertical scrollbar move that canvas once. There is no next-frame scroll mirroring between independent panes. Paired blank rows retain the alignment of additions and removals. Fixed row spacing agrees with the clipper's row height, preserving line navigation in long, scrolled comparisons.

Long source lines use one horizontal text offset in both columns. Their line numbers remain fixed and code/inline highlights clip inside each column. Column widths follow the actual visible canvas, so long text cannot push the other column offscreen. Unified mode uses the same canvas. Hunk/search navigation, selected rows, translated labels, source colors and Copy line remain available.

DiffState::scroll reports the current vertical position after input. Assigning a different value restores that position on the next call; focus continues to request row/hunk navigation. Distinct widget IDs keep independent canvas storage. Changing layouts does not create a second ImGui child or duplicate input handling.

pages.title: Quick filters for menus, panels and lists
pages.description: Quick filters for menus, panels and lists for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
Filtering is included in CyUI::Core and <cyui/Core.h>. It is opt-in per view: the host chooses which labeled controls, property rows or menu actions belong to the filter. Keep one TextFilter per panel/menu instance so independent views do not share queries. Dear ImGui is not patched, and raw ImGui calls are not automatically hidden.

Panel and list filtering#

cpp
// Persist alongside the panel's other state.cyui::TextFilter filter; // During the frame, inside the panel's ImGui window:cyui::panelHeader(cyui::tr("Properties").c_str(), nullptr, &filter);if (cyui::beginProperties("##properties")) {    if (filter.matches("Opacity", "Surface")) {        cyui::property(cyui::tr("Opacity").c_str());        cyui::sliderBar("##opacity", &opacity, 0, 1, "%.2f", -1);    }    cyui::endProperties();}

For a list, draw filterBox("##find", filter) and render matching rows from the host's model. filterBox returns whether the query changed. FilterOptions provides a translated hint, screen-pixel width, shortcut behavior, and optional focus/reset when the window appears. A zero width fills the row.

Ctrl+F focuses the field in the focused view (Cmd+F with ImGui's macOS behavior). The shortcut does not steal focus while another text editor accepts input; applications can call filter.focus() from their own shortcut routing. Escape inside the filter clears it, as does its clear button. Existing widgets outside the host's match conditions remain usable.

matches requires every whitespace-separated word to appear across the visible English label, its current translation and the supplied keywords. Match order does not matter. ASCII/Latin case, Latin accents/ligatures and combining accents are folded, so rugosite finds French Rugosité, and roughness still finds the same property. Other UTF-8 text is preserved; this is not full Unicode case folding. Keywords are searched as supplied: include translated keywords or paths when appropriate. Hidden ## and ### label identities are not indexed.

Collapsible sections and Inspector#

cpp
cyui::InspectorOptions options{&filter, "Surface"};const bool any = std::any_of(fields.begin(), fields.end(), [&](const auto& field) {    return cyui::propertyMatches(filter, field, "Surface");});if (cyui::beginFilteredSection("Surface", filter, any)) {    for (const auto& event : cyui::inspector("##surface", state, fields, revision,                                            validator, options)) {        handlePropertyEdit(event);    }    cyui::endSection();}

Matching sections open temporarily while filtering. Clearing the query restores their stored collapse preference. Include ancestor section names in row contexts so a section query keeps its children visible. Filtered Inspector rows retain their property IDs, draft values and host validation behavior; an active edit hidden by the filter emits a cancel proposal. Supply the full property model to Inspector rather than removing rows from its input.

Property matching considers names, translated help and section context, not property values or passwords. If the host stops calling Inspector for an entire hidden section/panel, it must cancel that section's outstanding previews itself. Clearing a filter never modifies the application's model.

Searchable menus#

cpp
cyui::TextFilter menuFilter; // persistent with this menu's statestd::vector<cyui::FilterMenuItem> entries{    {1, "Save", "Ctrl+S"},    {0, "Export", {}, {}, true, false, {        {2, "Export PNG", {}, "image texture"},        {3, "Export HDR", {}, "image", false}}}};if (ImGui::BeginMenu(cyui::trLabel("File").c_str())) {    const auto action = cyui::filterMenu("##file", menuFilter, entries);    if (action) dispatchAction(action);    ImGui::EndMenu();}

An item with children is a submenu; a zero-ID item with no label/children is a separator. Actions need unique nonzero 64-bit IDs. The host owns checked/enabled states and executes the returned ID. No filesystem, command execution or application callbacks are run by the filter.

With no query, the original nested menu is drawn. A query reveals matching descendant actions with translated breadcrumb paths. A parent title or keyword can match its descendants, and multiple words can match across the path and leaf caption. Disabled parents keep their results disabled. FilterMenuOptions controls design-unit width, reset and focus on opening; disable reset/focus when embedding the same function inline in a panel. filterMenuMatches(entries, filter) returns a snapshot for custom renderers without drawing UI.

Python#

python
import cyui as cfrom cyui_modules.inspector import inspector query = c.TextFilter()  # persistentc.panel_header(c.tr('Properties'), filter_state=query)for key, edit in inspector('details', state, properties, filter_state=query,                            filter_context='Surface'):    handle_edit(key, edit) entries = [c.FilterMenuItem(1, 'Save', 'Ctrl+S')]# Inside an open imgui menu or popup:action = c.filter_menu('file', menu_query, entries)

cyui_modules.filters also imports without ImGui for model-only matching. The APIs mirror C++ as filter_box, begin_filtered_section, filter_menu, filter_menu_matches and fold_filter_text. Python Inspector accepts filter_state and filter_context keyword arguments. The host handles data edits and cancellation in the same way as C++.

For large models, cache match results when the query, language or model revision changes, then clip the visible rows. No automatic search index or global view registry is maintained. Web content inside CEF remains owned by its Web app; the native filter does not rewrite an HTML document.

The C++ gallery's Filtering page (21), Details page (12), and Python gallery show these APIs. All controls use the shared palette, DPI sizes and English/French catalogs. Unreal panels can use the same Core functions in their draw callback.

pages.title: Local and contextual help
pages.description: Open a precise page without a server or browser dependency in Core.
pages.html:
Open the manual#

Keep the complete Documentation folder next to cyui_demo.exe. The Help menu opens it in the current language. F1 also works in the gallery-only view. The application resolves from its executable, not the working directory. A missing manual produces a readable error with the expected file.

The host owns browser launching: Core adds no web engine. Unreal tools can copy the export and launch its URI through their plugin’s mechanism; existing Unreal shortcuts are not globally intercepted.

Address contract#

IDs do not depend on translated headings. Use a file URI encoded by the platform path API (Path.as_uri in Python, UrlCreateFromPathW in the Windows demo), then append encoded route components:

text
Documentation.html#/en/integration/startupDocumentation.html#/fr/filtering/searchable-menusDocumentation.html#/fr/overview?media=workspace&zoom=1.5

Python helper#

The helper imports no ImGui and launches nothing on import. It resolves packaged resources from an installed wheel, or accepts a host-supplied manual path. Unknown languages fall back to en; missing page/section targets raise ValueError.

python
from cyui_modules.help import documentation_url, open_documentationurl = documentation_url('integration', 'startup', locale='fr')open_documentation('filtering', 'searchable-menus', locale='fr')

Legacy links#

Former docs Markdown files link to their matching reader pages. guide.html and fr/guide.html convert their ten former chapter fragments into CyDoc routes, with an ordinary link when JavaScript is disabled. CyDoc preserves start/editors/data/media/platforms page aliases. External links are optional reading references.

pages.title: Integrate CyUI
pages.html:
Localization is required for interface text: keep English as the default and French as the second built-in language. Read LOCALIZATION.md. Use cyui::trLabel("English label") for controls/tabs/windows and cyui::tr("English text") for display text. Register the application's messages and provide a language choice; do not translate user content, paths or IDs. Core includes localization automatically, without an extra module dependency.

Requirements: Dear ImGui 1.92 or newer (the docking branch is recommended) and C++17 (C++20 when CodeEditor or the optional CEF adapter is selected).

CMake#

cmake
set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET <the app's imgui target>)   # e.g. cydaw_imguiadd_subdirectory(external/CyUI ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/cyui)target_link_libraries(<app> PRIVATE CyUI::CyUI)

CyUI::CyUI is the compatibility umbrella. For selective integration use <cyui/Core.h> and CyUI::Core. Audio controls live in <cyui/modules/Audio.h> / CyUI::Audio; the gallery and theme editor live in <cyui/Gallery.h> / CyUI::Gallery. Audio and Gallery default to enabled; disable CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO / CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY when not needed, and disable CYUI_BUILD_DEMO for a selective build. Core never links those modules. See MODULES.md for complete examples, the implemented optional targets and their exact dependency boundaries.

For example, a source-reading application selects only Code and Diff:

cmake
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "Code;Diff" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)# add_subdirectory(...) after these optionstarget_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::Diff)

Without CMake#

Add include/ to the include path. Compile src/Theme.cpp, src/Widgets.cpp, src/Layout.cpp, src/Filter.cpp alongside the app's ImGui sources for Core. Add src/modules/Audio.cpp for audio controls, and src/Gallery.cpp for the gallery. Define CYUI_HAS_AUDIO=1 when compiling Gallery with audio examples.

Startup#

Do this after ImGui::CreateContext(), before the first NewFrame, and instead of the app's old theme function (ImGui::StyleColorsDark, ApplyTheme, a hand-written style.Colors[...] block):

cpp
#include <cyui/CyUI.h> cyui::Config config;config.themeKey = "mid-grey";            // see the theme table belowconfig.density  = cyui::Density::compact; // or comfortableconfig.dpiScale = dpiScale;              // 1.0 at 96 dpicyui::apply(config);cyui::loadFonts();                       // Segoe UI + Semibold + Consolas + MDL2 icons

When the DPI changes (WM_DPICHANGED), call cyui::applyDpi(newScale). It does nothing when the scale is unchanged. apply and a real DPI change rebuild the whole ImGuiStyle, so make your own style tweaks after them. At the end of every frame, after everything else, call cyui::renderNotifications(). It draws the toasts.

Config also has squareWindows: square, opaque windows for apps whose ImGui windows are OS windows (multi-viewports, plug-in editors). FontConfig has size (0: the density's font size), fallbackFolder (a folder of Inter, Roboto, JetBrains Mono or Cousine .ttf files, tried when the Windows fonts are missing) and icons (merge Segoe MDL2 Assets; on by default).

Several ImGui contexts (plug-in windows, editor panels): everything CyUI keeps is per context and released when the context is destroyed. That covers the palette, theme key, density, DPI, fonts, typed entry and toasts. Call apply and loadFonts with each context current. Theme calls change the current context only. With no context current, setPalette, setTheme and setDensity change every live context, and the defaults new contexts start from. Make such calls while no other thread draws with those contexts. apply and applyDpi with no context current change the defaults only.

themeKey look
mid-grey Mid greys, orange accent (default)
light-grey Light greys, dark text, orange accent
amber-night Deep blue-greys, amber accent
violet Dark slate, violet accent, cyan info
navy Deep navy, blue accent, flat

Use compact density for dense pro tools (DAW, editors). Use comfortable for launchers, hubs and settings-heavy apps.

pages.title: Licensing and commercial distribution
pages.description: Licensing and commercial distribution for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
CyUI is MIT licensed, including its optional first-party modules and the CEF / ImGuizmo adapters. The root license permits commercial use, modification, redistribution and sublicensing, subject to retaining its copyright and permission notice. It does not require an application's own source to be public.

Keep THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the notices for the dependencies actually included in your distribution. The bundled Dear ImGui and TextEditor code retain their MIT notices, as do the stb headers inside the Dear ImGui copy (imstb_*.h, MIT or public domain). CMake links that Dear ImGui copy whenever the host does not name its own target in CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET. Optional host dependencies retain their own licenses; they are not covered by CyUI's MIT grant.

For CEF, ship the license and Chromium credits/component notices belonging to the exact runtime build. Check separately any additional codec/media packages chosen by the application. CEF and its binary distribution are external dependencies, not a browser engine relicensed under MIT by CyUI.

CyMD, CyAnnota, CyTask and other surveyed applications have independent licenses, including GPL/AGPL in several repositories. Their source/assets are not copied into CyUI. The optional browser bridge implements message transport and the documented CyMD integration protocol. Loading or redistributing a separate Cy* application does not change that application's license to MIT. Decide which external applications to bundle under their own terms.

All new shared presentation implementations are written in CyUI against neutral models/callbacks. The MIT-licensed TextEditor snapshot retains its original license and recorded hashes. The CyDoc reader and its selected image/gallery modules are MIT; its notice is shipped in DocData/CyDoc-LICENSE.txt.

pages.title: Localization
pages.html:
Localization is part of Core, with no optional dependency. English (en) is the default language; French (fr) is built in. Built-in module controls use this catalog, and the C++ and Python galleries provide a live language selector. The same messages are available to embedded Web views.

C++#

Include <cyui/Core.h> or <cyui/Locale.h>. Choose a language after creating the view's ImGui context, before drawing its widgets:

cpp
cyui::setLocale("fr");                 // omit to keep Englishif (cyui::primaryButton(cyui::trLabel("Save").c_str()))    saveDocument();cyui::text("%s", cyui::tr("Ready").c_str());

Use tr for displayed text and trLabel for interactive labels, window titles, tabs and menus. trLabel("Save") displays the translated caption and retains the original ImGui identity. Explicit ###id and ##suffix identities are preserved too. Switching languages therefore keeps selection, focus and edits. Do not concatenate a translated caption into a new widget ID.

Applications can merge their own messages or register another language:

cpp
cyui::registerTranslations("fr", {{"app.export", "Exporter"}});cyui::registerTranslations("de", {{"Save", "Speichern"}}, "Deutsch");if (cyui::button(cyui::trLabel("app.export", "Export").c_str()))    exportDocument();

availableLocales() lists English, French, then additional registered languages. locale() returns the active code. Tags are normalized (fr_CA becomes fr-ca); an unregistered regional tag falls back to its registered language (fr-ca to fr). A missing message falls back to the base language, a registered English message, the supplied English fallback, then the key. setLocale returns false for an unavailable language and preserves the current one.

The active C++ language belongs to the current ImGui context. Catalogs are shared. With no context current, setLocale updates the defaults and existing contexts; do this only while other contexts are not rendering. Register catalogs outside concurrent rendering as well. Destroying a context releases its locale state. Store returned strings if their c_str() must outlive a function call; do not retain a pointer to a temporary translation in a model or callback.

Python#

The API is available through cyui, or without ImGui through cyui_modules.locale:

python
import cyui as cc.set_locale('fr')if c.primary_button(c.tr_label('Save')):    save_document()c.register_translations('fr', {'app.export': 'Exporter'})label = c.tr('app.export', 'Export')

available_locales() returns (code, name) pairs. locale_scope('fr') temporarily selects a language and restores it on exit. Python uses ContextVar state, so the locale belongs to the execution context, not an ImGui pointer. Tools sharing a Python context can use locale_scope around each view; independent async tasks may select their own language. Catalogs are shared within the Python interpreter.

Web and TypeScript#

createCyUIBridge() exposes an independent bridge.i18n catalog. Native webThemeJson() and Python theme_message() include the active locale. Send the theme again after changing language, or send a locale message with payload: {locale: 'fr'} using the normal versioned bridge envelope.

html
<button data-cyui-i18n="Save">Save</button><input data-cyui-i18n-placeholder="Search...">

The bridge translates marked interface text and placeholders and updates the document language. It leaves unmarked document content and input values alone. For framework components, use bridge.i18n.tr(key, englishFallback) in the framework's render/update cycle. createCyUILocale() also works without the native bridge. Adding messages or calling setLocale directly requires a new apply() or framework render; incoming native language messages call apply(). Copy cyui-i18n.js and cyui-locales.js with cyui-web.js when bundling the Web bridge. An iframe has its own language and must receive it through its own protocol; mountCyMD().open(name, file, locale) defaults to English.

Unreal Editor#

Call cyui::setLocale inside the panel's RunInContext callback, or from its draw callback. Each panel owns a context and can select a different language. Register application catalogs during tool setup. Native Slate/Unreal menu entries use Unreal's localization system; CyUI translates the content drawn by CyUI.

What applications translate#

CyUI supplies translations for its own controls, default prompts and gallery interface. Applications supply translations for their actions, validation messages and model captions. Inspector property names/help and choice captions, combo/segmented options, command captions/categories, field prompts, knob captions and tooltips use the catalog; their stored values and identifiers do not change. Pass English message keys or registered application keys for these captions.

Free text, file names, asset names, graph contents, source code, diffs, logs, documents and chat messages remain application data. They are not automatically translated. Format user content with a fixed format string, such as cyui::text("%s", content.c_str()). Persist the user's language preference in the application and apply it at startup; CyUI does not choose from the OS language.

Text is UTF-8. The host must load fonts covering the languages it enables; the Windows demo's fonts cover English and French. CyUI does not supply general right-to-left layout, complex-script shaping, plural rules or locale-specific date/number formatting. Those require host support or a dedicated text/formatting library. English/French UI translation does not imply those features.

pages.title: Module API and recipes
pages.description: Module API and recipes for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
All headers below use the cyui/ prefix. Link the corresponding target described in MODULES.md. The examples for every widget are in Gallery.cpp, tabs 4–19; the optional 3D adapter example appears in Viewport when enabled. Use the same palette/dp/style rules as Core for host callbacks and overlays.

IDs, state and edits#

Interaction.h defines ItemId (uint64), Point (double x/y), Range (min/max), Rect (screen bounds), borrowed ArrayView<T> and Edit<T>. Zero is reserved for no object. ItemScope includes all 64 ID bits in the ImGui stack. Own one state per panel, not one static gesture shared by every document. snapValue rounds symmetrically; zoomRange keeps the pointer anchor fixed.

Interactive model editors return begin/update/commit/cancel proposals. Apply a commit to the application model and record one Undo transaction. A revision change cancels a stale active edit; advance it when the external model is replaced. Atomic actions can commit immediately. Do not overwrite the external model with all preview updates unless the application deliberately owns that preview layer.

cpp
cyui::CurveState state;                   // persist with the panelstd::vector<cyui::CurvePoint> points;      // sorted, finite, stable nonzero IDscyui::CurveOptions options;options.revision = document.revision;options.snap = 0.25;auto edit = cyui::curveEditor("##automation", state, points, cyui::dp(0, 260), options);if (edit.committed()) document.commitCurve(edit.value);

The diagram/model types contain no engine pointers, JUCE strings or mandatory JSON types. Keep arrays and callback captures alive for the duration of a draw.

Canvas and numeric plots#

API Use
CanvasView::world/screen/zoomAt/fit Double world coordinates and anchored transforms
CanvasScope(id, state, size, options) / frame() Reserve a canvas, draw its background/grid and scope clipping; frame().wheel when navigation or claimWheel takes the wheel
drawCanvasGrid(rect, view, step) Grid overlay in the current window draw list
Axis::fraction/value Inverse linear/log mapping; logarithmic values require positive bounds
plot(id, PlotState&, ArrayView<PlotSeries>, size, options) Line/step/points/bars, ticks, legend, pan/zoom, crosshair and nearest sample ID/index
reducePlot(points, budget) Prepare min/max buckets, retaining spikes and conservative gaps
histogram(values, range, bins) uint64 counts, inclusive endpoints; ignores NaN/outside values
heatmap(id, values, columns, rows, valueRange, size) Bounded cells, missing-data color and hovered row/column

Canvas: middle drag or Space+left pans, wheel zooms at the pointer. Plot: middle drag pans, wheel zooms X, Ctrl-wheel also zooms Y. PlotOptions controls grid, axes, legend, crosshair/navigation, maxPoints and optional formatX/formatY callbacks for host units. Ticks and legend are drawn inside the plot bounds. Reported skippedSeries must prompt host reduction/querying; oversized data is not silently reduced every frame. Prepare/cache a bounded visible dataset outside draw.

cpp
cyui::PlotState state{{{20, 20000}, true}, {{-90, 0}, false}};cyui::PlotSeries line{1, "Spectrum", preparedPoints, cyui::PlotStyle::line, 1};cyui::PlotOptions options;options.formatX = [](double hz) { return formatFrequency(hz); };auto hover = cyui::plot("##response", state, {&line, 1}, cyui::dp(0, 220), options);

Curves, graphs and timeline#

API Use / result
evaluateCurve(points, time, fallback) Linear, step, smooth or Bezier evaluation of sorted keys
curveEditor(id, CurveState&, points, size, options) Editable points/handles and vector edit proposals
arrangeNodes(nodes, links, spacing) Deterministic layered positions; returns proposals, tolerates cycles
nodeEditor(id, NodeState&, nodes, links, size, options) Move vectors, connectFrom/connectTo, removeNodes/removeLink requests
timeline(id, TimelineState&, lanes, clips, markers, size, options) Clip move/trim edits, seek, range selection and remove IDs

Curve: double-click adds/removes keys; drag a point/selected Bezier handle; Ctrl extends selection, box-select blank space; Ctrl+A/C/V, Delete, Escape are scoped to the focused panel. Ctrl controls host/application shortcuts through ImGui's focus state. CurveOptions.evaluate evaluates the preview with host interpolation; snapTime can override the default snapping grid.

Nodes: drag cards or pins; Ctrl/Shift multi-select; blank drag box-selects; Home frames the graph; Delete proposes removing selected nodes; right-click a link in empty space proposes unlinking. canConnect(from,to) validates host pin types and connection rules before emitting a connect request. drawBody draws host details inside a card; it does not run the graph. The host removes dangling links when deleting nodes and allocates IDs for accepted new links.

The gallery's image graph uses NodeOptions::drawBody and a taller row to draw an image below a card's pin labels. Texture IDs come from the host through GalleryResources::imagePreviews (four optional previews); the host must keep them alive while the gallery draws. Assets uses the same textures as thumbnails, and Inspector uses one as an example object preview. These resources are optional: other hosts and tests show placeholders when no image is supplied. The demo's generated image pixels are sample data, independent of UI palette colors.

Timeline: wheel zooms at the pointer, Shift-wheel pans, Ctrl-wheel scrolls lanes; drag clips or their edges to move/trim. Locked clips/readOnly are respected. Blank drag selects a time interval; the ruler requests seeking. TimelineOptions supplies playhead, snap/minDuration, revision, formatTime, snapTime and drawClip. Time units and frame/sample rounding remain the application's responsibility.

Audio controls and prepared signal views#

modules/Audio.h retains knob/fader/meter and meterPosition. A fader spreads its own minimumDb..maximumDb over its travel (size 0 or negative follows ImGui sizing). The separate AudioViews target offers:

API Input
makePeaks(samples, columns) Min/max envelope preparation, preserving missing-only buckets as NaN
waveform(id, WaveformState&, WaveformData, playhead, size) Coverage interval plus prepared per-channel peak arrays
spectrum(id, PlotState&, series, size[, PlotOptions]) Frequency/value series, logarithmic X (invalid X resets to 20..20000)
oscilloscope(id, PlotState&, series, size[, PlotOptions]) Prepared time/amplitude series
stereoScope(id, PlotState&, series, size[, PlotOptions]) Square X/Y scope; both axes share one range symmetric around 0

Waveform emits seek/range-selection state, supports wheel zoom, Shift-wheel pan and middle drag. Decode audio, query envelope caches and compute FFT/DSP on the host side. Keep raw float audio ownership and thread synchronization out of draw.

Code, editing and Git-style diff presentation#

CodeDocument::setText(text, language, revision) preserves original UTF-8 bytes, tabs, CRLF and final-newline state. Display lines expand tabs to four columns and carry lexical spans. Languages include plain, C++, C#, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, GLSL, HLSL, JSON, Lua, SQL, INI and Markdown. Lexical coloring is a presentation heuristic; supply semantic parser/LSP results as overlays when needed.

  • setOverlays(SourceSpan[], revision) accepts zero-based lines and raw UTF-8 byte offsets. Stale revisions and offsets inside a code point are rejected.
  • tokenColor(role, background) maps token roles through the current palette, adjusting toward the text role for contrast. paintCodeLine draws prepared spans.
  • codeViewer(id, CodeViewState&, document, size, annotations) provides line numbers, search/next, selected/focused line, annotation hover and navigation IDs.
  • CodeEditor::setText/text/setLanguage/setReadOnly/draw wraps the optional MIT native TextEditor. draw returns document-changed. native() exposes advanced TextEditor hooks for completion, annotations, cursors, wrapping and Undo/Redo; include TextEditor.h and handle document storage/revisions in the host.
  • DiffDocument::setTexts(before, after, language, workBudget) prepares a bounded comparison; setUnified(text, language) reads a unified patch. rows, pairs, hunks, columns, revision, approximate expose prepared presentation data.
  • diffViewer(id, DiffState&, document, size) offers unified/side-by-side modes, one shared vertical canvas for both columns, a shared horizontal text offset with fixed line-number gutters, hunk/search navigation, inline changed ranges and old/new line navigation results. Final-newline-only changes are represented; CRLF and LF lines compare equal, with a notice row when line endings differ. DiffState::scroll reports the current vertical offset; assigning it requests a scroll. Hosts should call this viewer directly, without mirroring child-window offsets. See DIFF.md for details and native regression coverage.
  • expandTabs(text, tabSize) widens tabs to the next stop as displayed; displayOffset(raw, byteOffset, tabSize) maps a raw byte offset to that display text.
cpp
cyui::DiffDocument comparison;comparison.setTexts(beforeText, afterText, cyui::CodeLanguage::cpp);cyui::DiffState view;auto clicked = cyui::diffViewer("##comparison", view, comparison, cyui::dp(0, 400));if (clicked.newLine > 0) host.openNewDocumentAt(clicked.newLine);

Do not call setTexts on unchanged large documents every frame. Code and Diff do not depend on Git, LSP, a compiler or CodeEditor. Host repository/authentication, review comments, merge resolution and actions stay outside the renderer.

Inspector and assets#

Property supports bool, int64, double, strings, choices, readOnly/password/ multiline flags and optional bounds. Set integerMinimum/integerMaximum for exact integer bounds; do not convert int64 through double. inspector(id, state, properties, revision, validator) returns PropertyEdit entries. The validator returns an error string; invalid drafts remain visible without committing.

assetBrowser(id, AssetState&, items, size) uses AssetItem{id,parent,label,type, thumbnail,folder,favorite}. State owns query, folder, selected IDs and grid/list mode. It returns open/favorite/rename/remove requests. It performs no filesystem operation. CYUI_ASSET carries the stable numeric ID for host drag/drop handling. Folder parents and thumbnails are host data; querying/scanning/loading stays outside.

Images, viewport and optional 3D gizmo#

API Use
imageViewport(id, ImageState&, ImageData, size, ImageTool) Texture/UV crop, checkerboard, fit/zoom/pan, pixel hover and crop edit proposal
sampleGradient(stops, position, linearLight) Sample unordered stops using sRGB or explicit linear-light interpolation
gradientEditor(id, GradientState&, stops, size, linearLight, revision) Select/drag/add/remove stops; returns edits
cameraPosition/cameraViewMatrix(OrbitCamera) Arbitrary up axis, column-major right-handed camera
viewport(id, ViewportState&, ImageData, size, navigation) Aspect-preserving scene texture, UV picking, camera interaction
transformGizmo(id, TransformState&, Transform2D, options) 2D move/scale/rotation overlay, projection/unprojection callbacks
gizmo3D(id, Gizmo3DState&, matrix, view, projection, rect, options) Optional host ImGuizmo adapter for column-major scene transforms

Image: wheel zooms, middle drag pans, double-click fits; the crop tool returns a rectangle, and Escape restores the previous selection. Gradient: double-click adds an interpolated stop, drag moves it, right-click removes a stop when more than two remain. Host color editors change stop colors. Texture lifetime, color management and document transforms remain host-owned.

The transform gizmo's handles are ImGui items: over a canvas (imageViewport, viewport, CanvasScope) they take the hover and the click, so nothing underneath reacts. Host items drawn over a canvas get the same by calling markCanvasOverlay() each frame. Viewport: Alt-left drag orbits, middle drag pans, wheel changes distance. Host renderers produce the texture; CyUI does not render a 3D scene. Transform2D rotation is radians. Ctrl snaps rotation to 15-degree increments. Gizmo3DOptions selects ImGuizmo operation/mode, snap, orthographic view, revision and enabled state. Link CyUI::ImGuizmo only when a compatible host target is supplied.

Commands, logs and documents#

  • rankCommands(commands, query) matches every search word and returns stable ranked indices. commandPalette(id, open, state, commands, size) displays a modal palette with keyboard navigation and returns a requested command ID. Disabled entries do not execute; the host maps IDs to actions.
  • LogBuffer(capacity,maxBytes) provides synchronized append/clear/snapshot. logView(id, LogState&, buffer, size) filters/follows bounded cached rows and returns a selected ID; LogState.levels masks debug/info/warning/error. diagnosticList(id, rows, size) displays source/line/column/message and returns a requested diagnostic ID. The host resolves source navigation.
  • Document::setMarkdown caches a small renderer subset: headings, paragraphs, quotes, bullet/numbered items, rules, fenced code, links, inline code/emphasis and pipe tables. documentView(id, state, document, size) returns link/copy results. Links are returned to the host, not opened by the renderer.
  • transcript(id, TranscriptState&, messages, size) skips offscreen messages it has measured, caches Documents by message ID, follows appended/streamed content when at the bottom, and reports copy/link requests. Messages contain id/role/content/time. Full CyMD rendering can use Web.

The Markdown subset does not interpret raw HTML or run scripts. It intentionally uses the same Core widgets and Code colors. Native inline emphasis is a themed presentation subset rather than a complete CommonMark layout engine.

Optional Web / CEF#

webPanel, WebBackend/WebPlacement/WebInput, WebPolicy/webOrigin, webThemeJson and webEventJson form the engine-independent browser module. createWebCEF, webCEFApp and webCEFBrowser provide the optional CEF implementation. The browser draws in a host-owned texture and shares CyUI theme roles through CSS. See WEB.md for the complete lifecycle, native/Python recipes, TypeScript bridge, CyMD iframe protocol, origin checks, process sandbox and OS packaging. CEF is separate from Core and from the module's neutral API. The local validated runtime is Windows; Linux/macOS build/deployment validation is explicitly pending.

Rules when using it:

  • Pump CefDoMessageLoopWork() (Python runtime.pump()) outside the ImGui frame, before NewFrame. WebCEFOptions::upload and the optional release callback run inside it; release(texture) comes once after the browser closed: free that texture only after the frames that used it (Python: create(..., release=)).
  • external events are page requests, never commands. Only WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http/https) are reported; check userGesture, mainFrame and sourceOrigin, apply your own allow-list and ask the user before opening anything with the shell. Sub-frame popups without a gesture are dropped.
  • WebEventKind::dropped (data = count) reports events discarded by the queue caps (maxQueuedEvents, maxQueuedErrors for errors/console) or by policy.
  • WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot (taken on a false -> true change). A focused panel owns the keys it forwards, so ImGui nav and other widgets do not act on them.
  • Backend calls must run on the CEF UI thread; others are ignored. The supplied bridge, helper and demo run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (WEB.md "Process sandbox").

Python examples#

python
from cyui_modules.curves import CurvePoint, CurveState, curve_editorfrom cyui_modules.common import Range state = CurveState()state.view.x.view = Range(0, 10)state.view.y.view = Range(0, 1)points = [CurvePoint(1, 0, .2), CurvePoint(2, 10, .8)]# Each ImGui frame:edit = curve_editor('automation', state, points, (0, 260), revision=revision)if edit.committed:    points = edit.value

Python optional APIs are snake_case equivalents in the packages listed in MODULES.md. Python source offsets for SourceSpan are raw UTF-8 bytes; displayed lexer spans use Python character indices. Do not mix those two coordinate systems. CodeEditor in Python offers native ImGui multiline Undo plus a syntax preview; C++ TextEditor advanced callbacks are not exposed there. CEFRuntime is an explicit optional browser loader; importing model modules is independent of imgui-bundle, NumPy, audio/video or browser engines.

The separate AudioViews target offers: API Input makePeaks(samples, columns) Min/max envelope preparation, preserving missing-only buckets as NaN waveform(id, WaveformState&, WaveformData, playhead, size) Coverage interval plus prepared per-channel peak arrays spectrum(id, PlotState&, series, size[, PlotOptions]) Frequency/value series, logarithmic X (invalid X resets to 20..20000) oscilloscope(id, PlotState&, series, size[, PlotOptions]) Prepared time/amplitude series stereoScope(id, PlotState&, series, size[, PlotOptions]) Square X/Y scope; both axes share one range symmetric around 0 Waveform emits seek/range-selection state, supports wheel zoom, Shift-wheel pan and middle drag. Decode audio, query envelope caches and compute FFT/DSP on the host side. Keep raw float audio ownership and thread synchronization out of draw. Code, editing and Git-style diff presentation # CodeDocument::setText(text, language, revision) preserves original UTF-8 bytes, tabs, CRLF and final-newline state. Display lines expand tabs to four columns and carry lexical spans. Languages include plain, C++, C#, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, GLSL, HLSL, JSON, Lua, SQL, INI and Markdown. Lexical coloring is a presentation heuristic; supply semantic parser/LSP results as overlays when needed. setOverlays(SourceSpan[], revision) accepts zero-based lines and raw UTF-8 byte offsets. Stale revisions and offsets inside a code point are rejected. tokenColor(role, background) maps token roles through the current palette, adjusting toward the text role for contrast. paintCodeLine draws prepared spans. codeViewer(id, CodeViewState&, document, size, annotations) provides line numbers, search/next, selected/focused line, annotation hover and navigation IDs. CodeEditor::setText/text/setLanguage/setReadOnly/draw wraps the optional MIT native TextEditor. draw returns document-changed. native() exposes advanced TextEditor hooks for completion, annotations, cursors, wrapping and Undo/Redo; include TextEditor.h and handle document storage/revisions in the host. DiffDocument::setTexts(before, after, language, workBudget) prepares a bounded comparison; setUnified(text, language) reads a unified patch. rows , pairs , hunks , columns , revision , approximate expose prepared presentation data. diffViewer(id, DiffState&, document, size) offers unified/side-by-side modes, one shared vertical canvas for both columns, a shared horizontal text offset with fixed line-number gutters, hunk/search navigation, inline changed ranges and old/new line navigation results. Final-newline-only changes are represented; CRLF and LF lines compare equal, with a notice row when line endings differ. DiffState::scroll reports the current vertical offset; assigning it requests a scroll. Hosts should call this viewer directly, without mirroring child-window offsets. See DIFF.md for details and native regression coverage. expandTabs(text, tabSize) widens tabs to the next stop as displayed; displayOffset(raw, byteOffset, tabSize) maps a raw byte offset to that display text. cpp Copy cyui :: DiffDocument comparison ; comparison . setTexts ( beforeText , afterText , cyui :: CodeLanguage :: cpp ) ; cyui :: DiffState view ; auto clicked = cyui :: diffViewer ( "##comparison" , view , comparison , cyui :: dp ( 0 , 400 ) ) ; if ( clicked . newLine > 0 ) host . openNewDocumentAt ( clicked . newLine ) ; Do not call setTexts on unchanged large documents every frame. Code and Diff do not depend on Git, LSP, a compiler or CodeEditor. Host repository/authentication, review comments, merge resolution and actions stay outside the renderer. Inspector and assets # Property supports bool, int64, double, strings, choices, readOnly/password/ multiline flags and optional bounds. Set integerMinimum/integerMaximum for exact integer bounds; do not convert int64 through double. inspector(id, state, properties, revision, validator) returns PropertyEdit entries. The validator returns an error string; invalid drafts remain visible without committing. assetBrowser(id, AssetState&, items, size) uses AssetItem{id,parent,label,type, thumbnail,folder,favorite}. State owns query, folder, selected IDs and grid/list mode. It returns open/favorite/rename/remove requests. It performs no filesystem operation. CYUI_ASSET carries the stable numeric ID for host drag/drop handling. Folder parents and thumbnails are host data; querying/scanning/loading stays outside. Images, viewport and optional 3D gizmo # API Use imageViewport(id, ImageState&, ImageData, size, ImageTool) Texture/UV crop, checkerboard, fit/zoom/pan, pixel hover and crop edit proposal sampleGradient(stops, position, linearLight) Sample unordered stops using sRGB or explicit linear-light interpolation gradientEditor(id, GradientState&, stops, size, linearLight, revision) Select/drag/add/remove stops; returns edits cameraPosition/cameraViewMatrix(OrbitCamera) Arbitrary up axis, column-major right-handed camera viewport(id, ViewportState&, ImageData, size, navigation) Aspect-preserving scene texture, UV picking, camera interaction transformGizmo(id, TransformState&, Transform2D, options) 2D move/scale/rotation overlay, projection/unprojection callbacks gizmo3D(id, Gizmo3DState&, matrix, view, projection, rect, options) Optional host ImGuizmo adapter for column-major scene transforms Image: wheel zooms, middle drag pans, double-click fits; the crop tool returns a rectangle, and Escape restores the previous selection. Gradient: double-click adds an interpolated stop, drag moves it, right-click removes a stop when more than two remain. Host color editors change stop colors. Texture lifetime, color management and document transforms remain host-owned. The transform gizmo's handles are ImGui items: over a canvas (imageViewport, viewport, CanvasScope) they take the hover and the click, so nothing underneath reacts. Host items drawn over a canvas get the same by calling markCanvasOverlay() each frame. Viewport: Alt-left drag orbits, middle drag pans, wheel changes distance. Host renderers produce the texture; CyUI does not render a 3D scene. Transform2D rotation is radians. Ctrl snaps rotation to 15-degree increments. Gizmo3DOptions selects ImGuizmo operation/mode, snap, orthographic view, revision and enabled state. Link CyUI::ImGuizmo only when a compatible host target is supplied. Commands, logs and documents # rankCommands(commands, query) matches every search word and returns stable ranked indices. commandPalette(id, open, state, commands, size) displays a modal palette with keyboard navigation and returns a requested command ID. Disabled entries do not execute; the host maps IDs to actions. LogBuffer(capacity,maxBytes) provides synchronized append/clear/snapshot. logView(id, LogState&, buffer, size) filters/follows bounded cached rows and returns a selected ID; LogState.levels masks debug/info/warning/error. diagnosticList(id, rows, size) displays source/line/column/message and returns a requested diagnostic ID. The host resolves source navigation. Document::setMarkdown caches a small renderer subset: headings, paragraphs, quotes, bullet/numbered items, rules, fenced code, links, inline code/emphasis and pipe tables. documentView(id, state, document, size) returns link/copy results. Links are returned to the host, not opened by the renderer. transcript(id, TranscriptState&, messages, size) skips offscreen messages it has measured, caches Documents by message ID, follows appended/streamed content when at the bottom, and reports copy/link requests. Messages contain id/role/content/time. Full CyMD rendering can use Web. The Markdown subset does not interpret raw HTML or run scripts. It intentionally uses the same Core widgets and Code colors. Native inline emphasis is a themed presentation subset rather than a complete CommonMark layout engine. Optional Web / CEF # webPanel , WebBackend/WebPlacement/WebInput, WebPolicy/webOrigin, webThemeJson and webEventJson form the engine-independent browser module. createWebCEF , webCEFApp and webCEFBrowser provide the optional CEF implementation. The browser draws in a host-owned texture and shares CyUI theme roles through CSS. See WEB.md for the complete lifecycle, native/Python recipes, TypeScript bridge, CyMD iframe protocol, origin checks, process sandbox and OS packaging. CEF is separate from Core and from the module's neutral API. The local validated runtime is Windows; Linux/macOS build/deployment validation is explicitly pending. Rules when using it: Pump CefDoMessageLoopWork() (Python runtime.pump() ) outside the ImGui frame, before NewFrame . WebCEFOptions::upload and the optional release callback run inside it; release(texture) comes once after the browser closed: free that texture only after the frames that used it (Python: create(..., release=) ). external events are page requests, never commands. Only WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http/https) are reported; check userGesture , mainFrame and sourceOrigin , apply your own allow-list and ask the user before opening anything with the shell. Sub-frame popups without a gesture are dropped. WebEventKind::dropped (data = count) reports events discarded by the queue caps ( maxQueuedEvents , maxQueuedErrors for errors/console) or by policy. WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot (taken on a false -> true change). A focused panel owns the keys it forwards, so ImGui nav and other widgets do not act on them. Backend calls must run on the CEF UI thread; others are ignored. The supplied bridge, helper and demo run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (WEB.md "Process sandbox"). Python source offsets for SourceSpan are raw UTF-8 bytes; displayed lexer spans use Python character indices. Do not mix those two coordinate systems. CodeEditor in Python offers native ImGui multiline Undo plus a syntax preview; C++ TextEditor advanced callbacks are not exposed there. pages.title: Select optional modules
pages.description: Select optional modules for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
CyUI 1.2 provides a common Dear ImGui foundation and independently selectable interface modules. All CyUI code is MIT licensed. Applications own their models, engines, files, services, validation and Undo history.

Localization in every integration#

Core includes English (default), French and extensible translation catalogs. Use stable translated labels when migrating application interfaces. C++, Python, Web and Unreal usage, font requirements and host responsibilities are described in LOCALIZATION.md.

Targets and dependencies#

CyUI::Core contains themes, localization, quick filters, fonts, icons, ordinary widgets, layout and notifications. Modules link Core automatically. The following targets are implemented:

Menu/panel filtering is opt-in through Core's TextFilter, filterBox, filterMenu and the filtered panel header. Inspector accepts an optional filter without adding a dependency. See FILTERING.md.

CMake target Public header Interface Additional CyUI dependency
CyUI::Audio modules/Audio.h Knobs, faders, peak/RMS meters Core
CyUI::Canvas modules/Canvas.h Double coordinates, grid, clipping, pan/zoom Core
CyUI::Plots modules/Plots.h Linear/log axes, lines, steps, points, bars, histograms, heatmaps Canvas
CyUI::Curves modules/Curves.h Keyframes, Bezier handles, selection, snap, copy/paste Plots
CyUI::Nodes modules/Nodes.h Cards, pins, links, layout, move/connect/remove requests Canvas
CyUI::Timeline modules/Timeline.h Lanes, clips, markers, ruler, move/trim, range selection Canvas
CyUI::AudioViews modules/AudioViews.h Waveforms, spectrum, oscilloscope, stereo scope Plots
CyUI::Code modules/Code.h Source viewer, 102 syntax modes, extensible registry, semantic overlays, annotations, search Core + selected Lexilla engines + system threads
CyUI::Diff modules/Diff.h Unified/split diff, line numbers, hunk navigation, inline ranges Code
CyUI::CodeEditor modules/CodeEditor.h Native editable source, Undo/Redo, multiple cursors, completion hooks Code + MIT TextEditor, C++20
CyUI::Inspector modules/Inspector.h Typed properties, exact int64, validation, draft edits Core
CyUI::Assets modules/Assets.h Hierarchical folder navigation, grid/list, search, thumbnails, drag/drop Core
CyUI::Images modules/Images.h Texture viewport, checkerboard, crop, gradient stops Canvas
CyUI::Viewport modules/Viewport.h Host-rendered scene surface, orbit camera, 2D transform overlay Images
CyUI::Commands modules/Commands.h Searchable keyboard command palette Core
CyUI::Diagnostics modules/Diagnostics.h Bounded thread-safe logs, filters, diagnostic navigation Core + system threads
CyUI::DocumentViews modules/DocumentViews.h Markdown subset, fenced code, links, tables, cached transcripts Code
CyUI::Web modules/Web.h Browser panel, texture/input contract, origin policy, messages, theme bridge Core
CyUI::Gallery Gallery.h Examples and theme editor Enabled modules only

Header paths are relative to include/cyui/. CyUI::Code::Diff is an alias for CyUI::Diff. CyUI::CyUI is the compatibility umbrella linking all modules selected in this build. A module is a static library, not a dynamically loaded plugin.

Optional external adapters:

Target Enablement Dependency
CyUI::ImGuizmo Set CYUI_IMGUIZMO_TARGET to an existing host target; select Viewport Host's MIT ImGuizmo; adapters/ImGuizmo.h
CyUI::WebCEF CYUI_BUILD_WEB_CEF=ON; select Web Host CEF SDK/runtime; adapters/WebCEF.h, C++20

Neither adapter is downloaded or enabled by CYUI_MODULES=All. The Web module is usable with a host backend; the supplied browser implementation is CEF. See WEB.md for platform support, process lifecycle and deployment. WebCEF hands the host a texture release callback, reports external requests with userGesture/mainFrame/sourceOrigin (schemes limited by WebPolicy::externalSchemes) and counts discarded events in dropped events. The supplied bridge and helper run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (see WEB.md).

The optional Unreal Editor module packages selected CyUI modules for embedding in an existing plugin's Source/CyUI folder or sharing through one provider plugin. It provides a Slate renderer/input backend without menus or demo windows. Prepare it separately with tools/package_unreal.py --layout module (default); it is not a CMake target or a dependency of Core. A redistributed plugin embeds it under a unique name with --module-name, or depends on the shared provider.

Select only what an application needs#

cmake
set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui)set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "Code;Diff;Inspector" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::Diff CyUI::Inspector)
cpp
#include <cyui/Core.h>#include <cyui/modules/Diff.h>#include <cyui/modules/Inspector.h>

Dependencies are selected automatically: Diff enables Code; it does not enable CodeEditor, audio, plots or a browser. Link explicit targets to keep public feature macros and dependencies restricted to the consumer. CYUI_HAS_CODE, CYUI_HAS_DIFF, etc. are public definitions of their respective targets.

CYUI_MODULES accepts a semicolon list, Core, an empty list, or All. The standalone full demo defaults to All. Embedded builds and standalone builds with the demo disabled default to no new optional modules. Audio and Gallery retain their original ON defaults; disable those explicitly when not used. CyUI::Core never links them. The old Widgets.h/CyUI.h declarations remain source compatible.

Without CMake, compile the four Core sources and only the selected src/modules/<Name>.cpp files plus their dependency closure. Define the matching CYUI_HAS_<NAME> macros for Gallery/CyUI.h. CodeEditor also needs TextEditor.cpp, its include directory and C++20. Code and its dependents additionally compile src/modules/code/*.cpp, the bundled third_party/lexilla/lexlib/*.cxx and lexers/*.cxx, with Lexilla include/lexlib and Scintilla include directories. Define CYUI_CODE_LANGUAGE_CATALOGUE=1 for the extended C++ catalogue API. build_demo.bat is the complete Windows demo build.

Shared data and edit contract#

  • Give every object a stable, nonzero uint64 ID: results that return a bare ID (command palette, log/diagnostic rows, plot series, annotations) use 0 for none. Gestures track their targets with flags, so a 0 ID still drags and selects. Keep one state object per view.
  • Wheel zoom and pan keep ranges usable: a step that would overflow a log axis or shrink a span below what its magnitude resolves (|value| x 1e-12) is ignored. Selection ranges are reported ordered (min <= max).
  • ArrayView and callbacks borrow data for the call; keep it alive while drawing.
  • Curve points are finite and sorted by time; timeline durations are positive. Units, snapping policy, graph types and interpolation belong to the host.
  • Editors return Edit<T> proposals with begin, update, commit, cancel. Atomic actions may return commit directly. Preview state never mutates the host. Validate and apply a committed proposal as one Undo transaction. Increment the supplied revision when replacing host data during a gesture to cancel stale edits.
  • Ordinary rendering and model preparation run on the host UI thread. LogBuffer append/clear/snapshot are synchronized and may be called from producer threads.
  • Colors use palette roles; UI geometry uses dp/style. Gradient colors, plot values, textures and scene matrices are application data.
  • No module reads projects, executes Git actions, starts a terminal process, decodes audio/video, computes FFTs or runs a language server. Clipboard actions are local UI requests. Web explicitly creates a browser only when selected.

Prepare documents/envelopes when data changes. Draw visible rows using cached models, and supply visible/bounded datasets for graphs and timelines. Plots accept at most 65,536 points per series by default and report oversized IDs in skippedSeries; call reducePlot or query a host index before drawing. Heatmaps bound the displayed cells to 256 per axis. Diff uses patience anchors and bounded LCS (4 million cells by default), exposing approximate() when an unmatched region is displayed as a full replacement. Both source sides are retained; CRLF and LF lines compare equal and a notice row reports differing line endings. Source/Markdown inputs are limited to 32 MiB; large files need host paging. Logs default to 10,000 rows / 8 MiB. Waveforms consume prepared min/max envelopes.

Python#

sh
python -m pip install -e ".[ui]"

cyui remains the existing theme/widget API. cyui_modules contains optional audio, canvas, plots, curves, nodes, timeline, audioviews, code, diff, inspector, assets, images, viewport, commands, diagnostics, documents (documentviews alias), web and cef. Import models without loading imgui-bundle; drawing imports it lazily. No NumPy, media decoder or 3D engine is required.

Python uses the same IDs, ranges, palette roles, edit phases, origin policy and bounded diff algorithm. Its CodeEditor uses ImGui multiline editing with native Undo and a live syntax preview. The richer C++ TextEditor backend has its own API; Python does not pretend to expose its multiple cursors/completion hooks. cyui_modules.cef.CEFRuntime loads the optional C ABI library/helper explicitly; CEF binaries are not included in the Python package. See WEB.md.

pages.title: CyUI manual
pages.description: A common Dear ImGui foundation for C++ and Python desktop tools.
pages.html:
CyUI is a themed widget library on top of Dear ImGui 1.92+, with independently selectable C++ and Python interface modules. It serves developers of editors, creative tools and desktop utilities who need consistent controls, localization and specialized views. The host application keeps its renderer, data, engines and Undo history.

Start here#

  • Integrate CyUI with your existing ImGui target.
  • Choose modules and follow the shared edit contract.
  • Explore Core widgets, module recipes, localization and quick filters.
  • Use Python, Web/CEF or the optional Unreal Editor connector.
  • Read licensing before redistributing dependencies.

Explore the demo#

Extract the entire portable Windows ZIP, then run cyui_demo.exe. English is the default; Launch-French.cmd selects French. The gallery has live theme, density and language choices. Samples use synthetic data and generated preview textures. Its mixer, transport and project panels illustrate UI; they are not an audio engine, project system or complete editor.

sh
cyui_demo.exe --locale frcyui_demo.exe --theme violet --comfortablecyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 21cyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 7 --image-graph

The native gallery contains Text, Buttons, Controls, Containers, Canvas, Plots, Curves, Nodes, Timeline, Audio views, Code, Diff, Details, Assets, Images, Viewport, Commands, Diagnostics, Documents, Web, Layout and Filtering. The Web page needs a separately configured CEF backend for live browsing; the ordinary downloadable demo does not bundle CEF or Unreal.

Platforms and status#

The current version is 1.2.0. The project does not declare an alpha/beta label; development is active.

Component Availability
Core and ordinary C++ modules Portable sources for Windows/Linux/macOS; local MSVC build/render validation on Windows, cross-platform CI configured
Standalone demo Windows x64, Win32/DirectX 11; no Linux/macOS demo binary
Python Python 3.10+, imgui-bundle for drawing; model imports are renderer-independent
CEF adapter Optional SDK/runtime; Windows validated locally, Linux/macOS deployment requires target validation
Unreal connector Optional UE 5.5+ Editor C++; local UE 5.8.4 Windows validation, other targets require validation

Core is C++17. CodeEditor and the tested CEF SDK integration require C++20. The Windows demo uses system fonts; portable hosts supply fonts covering their languages. See integration and localization limits.

Read offline#

Open Documentation/Documentation.html directly from disk. Keep the complete Documentation folder together, including DocData. There is no server, CDN, account or Internet dependency. Optional reference links to external projects require a connection only when you choose to follow them.

F1 and Help → Documentation in the demo open this local manual in the current interface language. The Help menu also opens the module, filtering and localization chapters. In the Python gallery, use the Documentation button or F1 for the active module. Help integration describes the reusable Python helper and native routes.

Use the sidebar and its nested topics, or Ctrl+K to search prose, code and documented API symbols. A language change keeps page and explicit section IDs. Images and galleries enlarge inside the documentation window; Escape closes the enlarged view. Keyboard focus exposes controls, touch controls remain available, and session navigation retains reading positions. Personal annotations/preferences depend on the browser’s local storage permissions.

Explore the illustrated module tour.

pages.title: Python integration
pages.description: Install the Python UI, import models and run the module gallery.
pages.html:
Installation#

CyUI requires Python 3.10+. Install the checkout with python -m pip install -e ., or install its built wheel. imgui-bundle 1.92+ is the declared drawing dependency; the historical [ui] extra remains compatible. Model-only imports under cyui_modules do not import the renderer, media decoders, NumPy or CEF.

python
from cyui_modules.common import Rangefrom cyui_modules.diff import DiffDocumentcomparison = DiffDocument()comparison.set_texts('old\n', 'new\n', 'plain')

Draw a gallery#

Run python examples/python_modules.py with imgui-bundle installed. Its ModuleGallery can also be embedded in your existing application. Create one gallery per host view, call draw during the GUI frame, and keep host textures/Web backends alive. Theme and language selectors update live; use the Documentation button or F1 for contextual help.

Use cyui.apply() once after context creation, cyui.set_locale('fr') for French, and cyui.render_notifications() once per frame. Follow the module edit recipes, translation scopes and filters.

Native and Python differences#

Python optional families use snake_case APIs. Its CodeEditor uses ImGui multiline editing, native Undo and a live syntax preview. The C++ TextEditor multiple cursors/completion hooks and native syntax-plugin registry are not Python bindings. Python SourceSpan offsets are UTF-8 bytes; displayed Python lexer spans use character indices. The Diff renderer is independent of the native C++ shared-canvas implementation.

CEF is explicitly loaded through CEFRuntime; its library, helpers and Chromium runtime are supplied separately. The Web guide explains thread, texture and shutdown ownership. The Python wheel includes the entire local manual as cyui_documentation package data; no Node.js is required to read it.
