pages.title: Reusable CyUI module for Unreal plugins
pages.description: Reusable CyUI module for Unreal plugins for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
CyUI is an optional Editor module that other Unreal plugins can embed or share. It supplies the CyUI/ImGui library, the Slate renderer, input, clipboard, font textures and Unreal texture registry. Loading the module creates no menus, demo tools or windows. Your plugin owns its layout, commands and state. Core/CMake/Python consumers do not acquire Unreal dependencies. This integration is for native C++ editor tools, not UMG, runtime gameplay UI or Blueprints.

Embed the module in an existing plugin#

Prepare a new staging directory (Python 3.10+):

sh
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --output build/unreal-module/CyUI --modules Core Plots Inspector Code Diff

module is the default layout. Copy that single CyUI folder to <YourPlugin>/Source/CyUI. It contains its Build.cs, public headers, private backend, selected library snapshot, dependencies and MIT notices. It requires no separate CyUI plugin and no external checkout path.

Append this entry to your plugin's existing .uplugin Modules array; the generated ModuleDescriptor.json contains the same entry. Keep your existing module entries:

json
{ "Name": "CyUI", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit" }

Add "CyUI" to the dependencies of your plugin's Editor module:

csharp
PrivateDependencyModuleNames.Add("CyUI");CppStandard = CppStandardVersion.Cpp20;

Use PublicDependencyModuleNames instead if your public headers expose CyUI types. Runtime/gameplay modules must not depend on this Editor module. Regenerate IDE project files and build the Editor target with UnrealBuildTool.

Inside the module, Library/src and third-party implementations retain their source bytes as .inl files. Generated .cpp bridges compile each exactly once; UBT's recursive source discovery cannot compile duplicate implementations. Header paths and the API remain unchanged. Library/SOURCE_LAYOUT.json records the original-to-packaged paths; the TextEditor hash manifest uses its packaged name. No engine code is copied. CYUI_API remains empty for static CMake integration.

A plugin you redistribute: unique module name#

Two enabled plugins that each embed a module named CyUI cannot load together: Unreal needs one definition per module name. A plugin distributed to others (a Marketplace/Fab or studio-wide tool) should therefore either depend on the shared provider plugin below, or embed a copy under its own module name:

sh
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --module-name MyToolCyUI --output build/unreal-module/MyToolCyUI --modules Core Plots

Copy the folder to <YourPlugin>/Source/MyToolCyUI, list { "Name": "MyToolCyUI", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit" } in your .uplugin and depend on "MyToolCyUI" in Build.cs. The script renames the Build.cs class/file, the folder, the descriptor and test names; the Build.cs defines CYUI_UNREAL_MODULE (used by IMPLEMENT_MODULE and FCyUIModule::Get()) and maps CYUI_API to MYTOOLCYUI_API. C++ class names and headers are unchanged.

Each embedded copy still contains its own Dear ImGui build and exports it (IMGUI_API=CYUI_API, public third_party/imgui include path). A consumer module must depend on exactly one CyUI module, and must not also use another ImGui plugin's headers. ImGui itself is not renamespaced: with two copies loaded, Windows keeps each DLL's symbols separate; Linux/macOS symbol resolution between two copies has not been validated.

Share one module between several plugins#

A project must contain one definition of the module named CyUI. To use several consumer plugins together, put the module in one common provider plugin and make the consumers depend on it. Do not copy Source/CyUI into each enabled plugin.

An optional provider container can be prepared with:

sh
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout plugin --output build/unreal-provider/CyUI --modules All --gallery

Copy it to <Project>/Plugins/CyUI. In each consuming plugin's .uplugin, append this reference to its existing Plugins array:

json
{ "Name": "CyUI", "Enabled": true }

The consumer's Build.cs still depends on the module CyUI. The provider plugin is only a container and adds no interface on its own. If your provider has a different plugin name, use that name in the Plugins reference; the module name in Build.cs remains CyUI (or the --module-name you packaged it with). Follow Unreal's project/engine dependency hierarchy.

--modules Core is minimal; All includes all ordinary CyUI modules. Dependencies are selected automatically. --gallery only includes the gallery API: your plugin chooses when to call it. CEF and external ImGuizmo are not packaged here. Existing output folders are refused. Prepare a new staging folder and replace the previous module deliberately with the editor closed. Restart after backend/library changes; the shared module disables dynamic unloading.

Complete consuming-plugin example#

examples/unreal/CyUIToolExample is a separate plugin with its own Build.cs, descriptor, Window-menu entry, nomad tab, Slate layout, CyUI draw callback and teardown. Its descriptor references the shared provider CyUI; enable this example only when you want its interface. It embeds a panel using MakePanel, not a stand-alone CyUI window. With Gallery selected, its own interface can open the gallery. For embedding in an existing plugin, copy the example's integration pattern and declare the module inside that plugin as described above.

Register an editor tool#

In your Editor module's .Build.cs:

csharp
PrivateDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new[] { "Core", "CyUI" });CppStandard = CppStandardVersion.Cpp20;

Register the tool in StartupModule, unregister it in ShutdownModule:

cpp
#include "CyUIModule.h"#include <cyui/Core.h> void FMyEditorTools::StartupModule(){    FCyUIModule::Get().RegisterTool(        "MyTools.Inspector", NSLOCTEXT("MyTools", "Inspector", "My CyUI Inspector"),        FOnDrawCyUITool::CreateRaw(this, &FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector));} void FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector(){    cyui::heading("My editor tool");    if (cyui::primaryButton("Inspect selection")) {        // Read the editor selection / request a host action here.    }} void FMyEditorTools::ShutdownModule(){    if (FCyUIModule::IsAvailable())        FCyUIModule::Get().UnregisterTool("MyTools.Inspector");}

RegisterTool rejects empty/duplicate IDs and unbound callbacks. OpenTool(id) opens the registered nomad tab. Your plugin adds its own menu/button/command to call OpenTool; the service does not add a Window menu. Unregistration detaches the callback before requesting tab closure, so a closed/unloading owner cannot keep drawing. For an existing Slate layout, MakePanel(callback) returns an SWidget. Keep the owning callback valid for its panel's lifetime; cast to SCyUIPanel and call Detach() before destroying a raw callback owner.

cpp
#include "CyUIModule.h"#include "SCyUIPanel.h" // During your toolkit/tab construction, keep this as an owning-plugin member:Panel = StaticCastSharedRef<SCyUIPanel>(FCyUIModule::Get().MakePanel(    FOnDrawCyUITool::CreateRaw(this, &FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector)));// Insert Panel.ToSharedRef() in a Slate slot or SDockTab content.// Before unloading the owning plugin:if (Panel) { Panel->Detach(); Panel.Reset(); }

CyUIModule.h exposes the FCyUIModule entry point. The older CyUIEditorModule.h / FCyUIEditorModule names remain compatible aliases/types.

Both methods accept an optional FOnInitializeCyUITool as their last argument. It runs once per newly created panel with its context current, after the default fonts are loaded and before the first frame. Use it to merge a host-supplied font into cyui::uiFont() (set ImFontConfig::MergeMode and DstFont) or configure additional fonts. SCyUIPanel exposes the same OnInitialize Slate argument. Unicode storage/input does not supply missing font glyphs: choose fonts covering the scripts your tool displays, with appropriate distribution rights.

The connector owns CreateContext, NewFrame, the root Begin/End, Render and notifications. The callback draws contents. Do not run another ImGui frame, destroy/change the context or load fonts from a draw callback. CyUI Gallery may create its own ordinary ImGui windows inside the panel. Native OS windows and docking belong to Slate; ImGui multi-viewport OS windows are disabled.

All APIs/callbacks run on the editor game thread. Work that changes assets or the world must use the owning Unreal tool's transactions, Modify, validation and Undo/Redo. Draw callbacks may run more than once per editor frame; execute actions on widget events rather than unconditionally. Read/prepare expensive data outside the paint callback.

Each panel owns an independent ImGui context. Numeric-entry buffers, wheel state and notifications are scoped to that context and released on context shutdown. Palette, density, DPI and fonts are per context too: a theme call styles the panel whose context is current (inside its draw/initialize callback), and a new panel starts from the defaults set by theme calls made while no ImGui context is current. From Slate handlers or other code outside the draw callback, use the panel helpers: Panel->RunInContext([] { cyui::setTheme("navy"); }), and Panel->Notify("Saved", cyui::Tone::success) (or cyui::notify(context, ...)). A plain cyui::notify() with no current context is dropped. Slate's render transform handles desktop DPI, while DisplayFramebufferScale supplies font rasterization density; the panel keeps CyUI's logical DPI at 1 and does not re-apply the style on every paint.

Input routing: each key goes to exactly one side. ImGui receives it (and Slate sees it handled) while ImGui takes keyboard input: an active item or text field, a modal, or a focused view that calls ImGui::SetNextFrameWantCaptureKeyboard(true) (as webPanel does); plain navigation keys (arrows, Tab, Space, Enter, Escape, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End) also go to ImGui while its keyboard navigation is active. Every other key goes only to Unreal, so editor shortcuts such as Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Delete or F7 work over the panel and never run twice. A tool with its own shortcuts (Delete, Ctrl+C/V in a canvas) must claim the keyboard that way while focused. Characters go to ImGui only while it takes keyboard input. The mouse wheel is sent as vertical; ImGui turns Shift+wheel into horizontal scrolling. ImGui's own textures (font atlas) are transient UTexture2Ds updated in place, only in the changed rectangle.

Show Unreal textures#

cpp
const uint64 imageId = FCyUIModule::Get().RegisterTexture(myTexture);// In the draw callback (or ImageData for CyUI::Images / Viewport):ImGui::Image(ImTextureRef(ImTextureID(imageId)), cyui::dp(256, 256));// After the tool stops submitting this image:FCyUIModule::Get().UnregisterTexture(imageId);

Registration holds a strong UObject reference. Unregistration finishes submitted Slate/render commands before releasing that reference; avoid doing it every paint. Register/unregister textures outside draw callbacks, after stopping submissions of the old image, for example in the owning tool's setup/teardown. ID 0 and stale/unregistered IDs are skipped. Texture IDs from other ImGui or RHI backends are not valid here. Only ordinary Slate-renderable UTexture resources are supported by this registry; custom GPU pipelines need their own adapter.

Compatibility and limits#

The connector targets Unreal Engine 5.5+ desktop editor builds on Windows/Linux/macOS through public Slate APIs. The locally validated installation is UE 5.8.4 on Windows x64. Other versions and platforms require validation on the target installation.

IME composition/candidate placement, accessibility text providers, touch/gamepad and OS-level ImGui multi-viewports are not implemented by this basic editor backend. Basic Unicode character events and clipboard text are supported. An existing third-party Unreal ImGui plugin may use a different ABI/context; do not share its headers, symbols or texture IDs with this connector.

The generic Web module may be selected, but WebCEF is not packaged into Unreal. Unreal may already load its own browser runtime; a Web backend for Unreal must follow that engine's browser lifecycle and version requirements.

CyUI's English/French localization is included through Core. Set the panel's language within RunInContext or its draw callback; separate panel contexts keep separate languages. Slate tool/menu entries still use Unreal localization. See LOCALIZATION.md for the catalog and stable-label API.

License#

CyUI's connector and packaging script remain MIT. Dear ImGui and the optional TextEditor retain their MIT notices. Unreal Engine remains an external dependency under Epic's own license; it is not redistributed or relicensed by CyUI. Preserve the plugin's LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES when distributing CyUI code.

API references: Slate editor window workflow, FSlateVertex, FSlateRenderer.

A plugin distributed to others (a Marketplace/Fab or studio-wide tool) should therefore either depend on the shared provider plugin below, or embed a copy under its own module name: sh Copy python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --module-name MyToolCyUI --output build/unreal-module/MyToolCyUI --modules Core Plots Copy the folder to <YourPlugin>/Source/MyToolCyUI , list { "Name": "MyToolCyUI", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit" } in your .uplugin and depend on "MyToolCyUI" in Build.cs. The script renames the Build.cs class/file, the folder, the descriptor and test names; the Build.cs defines CYUI_UNREAL_MODULE (used by IMPLEMENT_MODULE and FCyUIModule::Get() ) and maps CYUI_API to MYTOOLCYUI_API . C++ class names and headers are unchanged. Each embedded copy still contains its own Dear ImGui build and exports it ( IMGUI_API=CYUI_API , public third_party/imgui include path). A consumer module must depend on exactly one CyUI module, and must not also use another ImGui plugin's headers. ImGui itself is not renamespaced: with two copies loaded, Windows keeps each DLL's symbols separate; Linux/macOS symbol resolution between two copies has not been validated. Share one module between several plugins # A project must contain one definition of the module named CyUI . To use several consumer plugins together, put the module in one common provider plugin and make the consumers depend on it. Do not copy Source/CyUI into each enabled plugin. An optional provider container can be prepared with: sh Copy python tools/package_unreal.py --layout plugin --output build/unreal-provider/CyUI --modules All --gallery Copy it to <Project>/Plugins/CyUI . In each consuming plugin's .uplugin , append this reference to its existing Plugins array: json Copy { "Name" : "CyUI" , "Enabled" : true } The consumer's Build.cs still depends on the module CyUI . The provider plugin is only a container and adds no interface on its own. If your provider has a different plugin name, use that name in the Plugins reference; the module name in Build.cs remains CyUI (or the --module-name you packaged it with). Follow Unreal's project/engine dependency hierarchy. --modules Core is minimal; All includes all ordinary CyUI modules. Dependencies are selected automatically. --gallery only includes the gallery API: your plugin chooses when to call it. CEF and external ImGuizmo are not packaged here. Existing output folders are refused. Prepare a new staging folder and replace the previous module deliberately with the editor closed. Restart after backend/library changes; the shared module disables dynamic unloading. Complete consuming-plugin example # examples/unreal/CyUIToolExample is a separate plugin with its own Build.cs, descriptor, Window-menu entry, nomad tab, Slate layout, CyUI draw callback and teardown. Its descriptor references the shared provider CyUI ; enable this example only when you want its interface. It embeds a panel using MakePanel , not a stand-alone CyUI window. With Gallery selected, its own interface can open the gallery. For embedding in an existing plugin, copy the example's integration pattern and declare the module inside that plugin as described above. Register an editor tool # In your Editor module's .Build.cs : csharp Copy PrivateDependencyModuleNames . AddRange ( new [ ] { "Core" , "CyUI" } ) ; CppStandard = CppStandardVersion . Cpp20 ; Register the tool in StartupModule , unregister it in ShutdownModule : cpp Copy # include "CyUIModule.h" # include <cyui/Core.h> void FMyEditorTools :: StartupModule ( ) { FCyUIModule :: Get ( ) . RegisterTool ( "MyTools.Inspector" , NSLOCTEXT ( "MyTools" , "Inspector" , "My CyUI Inspector" ) , FOnDrawCyUITool :: CreateRaw ( this , & FMyEditorTools :: DrawInspector ) ) ; } void FMyEditorTools :: DrawInspector ( ) { cyui :: heading ( "My editor tool" ) ; if ( cyui :: primaryButton ( "Inspect selection" ) ) { // Read the editor selection / request a host action here. } } void FMyEditorTools :: ShutdownModule ( ) { if ( FCyUIModule :: IsAvailable ( ) ) FCyUIModule :: Get ( ) . UnregisterTool ( "MyTools.Inspector" ) ; } RegisterTool rejects empty/duplicate IDs and unbound callbacks. OpenTool(id) opens the registered nomad tab. Your plugin adds its own menu/button/command to call OpenTool; the service does not add a Window menu. Unregistration detaches the callback before requesting tab closure, so a closed/unloading owner cannot keep drawing. For an existing Slate layout, MakePanel(callback) returns an SWidget . Keep the owning callback valid for its panel's lifetime; cast to SCyUIPanel and call Detach() before destroying a raw callback owner. cpp Copy # include "CyUIModule.h" # include "SCyUIPanel.h" // During your toolkit/tab construction, keep this as an owning-plugin member: Panel = StaticCastSharedRef < SCyUIPanel > ( FCyUIModule :: Get ( ) . MakePanel ( FOnDrawCyUITool :: CreateRaw ( this , & FMyEditorTools :: DrawInspector ) ) ) ; // Insert Panel.ToSharedRef() in a Slate slot or SDockTab content. // Before unloading the owning plugin: if ( Panel ) { Panel -> Detach ( ) ; Panel . Reset ( ) ; } CyUIModule.h exposes the FCyUIModule entry point. The older CyUIEditorModule.h / FCyUIEditorModule names remain compatible aliases/types. Both methods accept an optional FOnInitializeCyUITool as their last argument. It runs once per newly created panel with its context current, after the default fonts are loaded and before the first frame. Use it to merge a host-supplied font into cyui::uiFont() (set ImFontConfig::MergeMode and DstFont ) or configure additional fonts. SCyUIPanel exposes the same OnInitialize Slate argument. Unicode storage/input does not supply missing font glyphs: choose fonts covering the scripts your tool displays, with appropriate distribution rights. The connector owns CreateContext , NewFrame , the root Begin/End , Render and notifications. The callback draws contents . Do not run another ImGui frame, destroy/change the context or load fonts from a draw callback. CyUI Gallery may create its own ordinary ImGui windows inside the panel. Native OS windows and docking belong to Slate; ImGui multi-viewport OS windows are disabled. All APIs/callbacks run on the editor game thread. Work that changes assets or the world must use the owning Unreal tool's transactions, Modify , validation and Undo/Redo. Draw callbacks may run more than once per editor frame; execute actions on widget events rather than unconditionally. Read/prepare expensive data outside the paint callback. Each panel owns an independent ImGui context. Numeric-entry buffers, wheel state and notifications are scoped to that context and released on context shutdown. Palette, density, DPI and fonts are per context too: a theme call styles the panel whose context is current (inside its draw/initialize callback), and a new panel starts from the defaults set by theme calls made while no ImGui context is current. From Slate handlers or other code outside the draw callback, use the panel helpers: Panel->RunInContext([] { cyui::setTheme("navy"); }) , and Panel->Notify("Saved", cyui::Tone::success) (or cyui::notify(context, ...) ). A plain cyui::notify() with no current context is dropped. Slate's render transform handles desktop DPI, while DisplayFramebufferScale supplies font rasterization density; the panel keeps CyUI's logical DPI at 1 and does not re-apply the style on every paint. Input routing: each key goes to exactly one side. ImGui receives it (and Slate sees it handled) while ImGui takes keyboard input: an active item or text field, a modal, or a focused view that calls ImGui::SetNextFrameWantCaptureKeyboard(true) (as webPanel does); plain navigation keys (arrows, Tab, Space, Enter, Escape, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End) also go to ImGui while its keyboard navigation is active. Every other key goes only to Unreal, so editor shortcuts such as Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Delete or F7 work over the panel and never run twice. A tool with its own shortcuts (Delete, Ctrl+C/V in a canvas) must claim the keyboard that way while focused. Characters go to ImGui only while it takes keyboard input. The mouse wheel is sent as vertical; ImGui turns Shift+wheel into horizontal scrolling. ImGui's own textures (font atlas) are transient UTexture2D s updated in place, only in the changed rectangle. Show Unreal textures # cpp Copy const uint64 imageId = FCyUIModule :: Get ( ) . RegisterTexture ( myTexture ) ; // In the draw callback (or ImageData for CyUI::Images / Viewport): ImGui :: Image ( ImTextureRef ( ImTextureID ( imageId ) ) , cyui :: dp ( 256 , 256 ) ) ; // After the tool stops submitting this image: FCyUIModule :: Get ( ) . UnregisterTexture ( imageId ) ; Registration holds a strong UObject reference. Unregistration finishes submitted Slate/render commands before releasing that reference; avoid doing it every paint. Register/unregister textures outside draw callbacks, after stopping submissions of the old image, for example in the owning tool's setup/teardown. ID 0 and stale/unregistered IDs are skipped. Texture IDs from other ImGui or RHI backends are not valid here. Only ordinary Slate-renderable UTexture resources are supported by this registry; custom GPU pipelines need their own adapter. Compatibility and limits # The connector targets Unreal Engine 5.5+ desktop editor builds on Windows/Linux/macOS through public Slate APIs. The locally validated installation is UE 5.8.4 on Windows x64. Other versions and platforms require validation on the target installation. IME composition/candidate placement, accessibility text providers, touch/gamepad and OS-level ImGui multi-viewports are not implemented by this basic editor backend. Basic Unicode character events and clipboard text are supported. An existing third-party Unreal ImGui plugin may use a different ABI/context; do not share its headers, symbols or texture IDs with this connector. The generic Web module may be selected, but WebCEF is not packaged into Unreal. Unreal may already load its own browser runtime; a Web backend for Unreal must follow that engine's browser lifecycle and version requirements. CyUI's English/French localization is included through Core. Set the panel's language within RunInContext or its draw callback; separate panel contexts keep separate languages. Slate tool/menu entries still use Unreal localization. See LOCALIZATION.md for the catalog and stable-label API. License # CyUI's connector and packaging script remain MIT. Dear ImGui and the optional TextEditor retain their MIT notices. Unreal Engine remains an external dependency under Epic's own license ; it is not redistributed or relicensed by CyUI. Preserve the plugin's LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES when distributing CyUI code. API references: Slate editor window workflow , FSlateVertex , FSlateRenderer . python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --output build/unreal-module/CyUI --modules Core Plots Inspector Code Diff { "Name": "CyUI", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit" } PrivateDependencyModuleNames.Add("CyUI"); CppStandard = CppStandardVersion.Cpp20; python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --module-name MyToolCyUI --output build/unreal-module/MyToolCyUI --modules Core Plots python tools/package_unreal.py --layout plugin --output build/unreal-provider/CyUI --modules All --gallery { "Name": "CyUI", "Enabled": true } PrivateDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new[] { "Core", "CyUI" }); } void FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector() { cyui::heading("My editor tool"); if (cyui::primaryButton("Inspect selection")) { // Read the editor selection / request a host action here. } } void FMyEditorTools::ShutdownModule() { if (FCyUIModule::IsAvailable()) FCyUIModule::Get().UnregisterTool("MyTools.Inspector"); } #include "CyUIModule.h" #include "SCyUIPanel.h" // During your toolkit/tab construction, keep this as an owning-plugin member: Panel = StaticCastSharedRef<SCyUIPanel>(FCyUIModule::Get().MakePanel( FOnDrawCyUITool::CreateRaw(this, &FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector))); // Insert Panel.ToSharedRef() in a Slate slot or SDockTab content. // Before unloading the owning plugin: if (Panel) { Panel->Detach(); Panel.Reset(); } const uint64 imageId = FCyUIModule::Get().RegisterTexture(myTexture); pages.title: Web panels with CEF
pages.description: Web panels with CEF for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
CyUI's optional Web module embeds HTML/CSS/JavaScript interfaces in a Dear ImGui panel. TypeScript is compiled to JavaScript by the web application's own build. The supplied browser engine is CEF, using off-screen rendering into a texture owned by the host renderer. This avoids a platform-native child window covering ImGui popups or docking panels. No browser dependency enters Core.

Platform and validation matrix#

Component Windows Linux macOS
Core and ordinary C++ modules Portable sources; MSVC build/tests/render checked locally Portable sources; CI configured, not run locally Portable sources; CI configured, not run locally
Python models / imgui-bundle UI Models and real ImGui frames checked locally Same Python sources; target environment needs validation Same Python sources; target environment needs validation
Web policy, messages, JS/TS declarations Tested Platform-independent code Platform-independent code
WebCEF off-screen adapter Compiled; real page, paint and native/Python message round trips tested Shared implementation; build/runtime packaging unverified here Shared implementation; framework/helper/AppKit packaging unverified here
Win32/DX11 demo and BMP capture Implemented and tested Host supplies its ImGui backend Host supplies its ImGui backend

CEF itself supplies Windows, Linux and macOS distributions. CyUI does not claim that adding a CMake option validates a finished application on all three systems. CEF was tested here with 150.0.23+g4ccc4ca+chromium-150.0.7871.287, Windows x64. Choose and validate a maintained CEF SDK for each target architecture.

Build selection#

cmake
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "Web" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_WEB_CEF ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_CEF_ROOT "path/to/extracted/cef_binary_distribution" CACHE PATH "" FORCE)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::WebCEF)

Alternatively set CYUI_CEF_TARGET to a host target providing the CEF headers, runtime library and C++ wrapper. This is useful when the application already owns CEF packaging. The adapter requires C++20 for the tested SDK. Core remains C++17. No SDK/runtime download happens during configure or drawing.

The build also creates cyui_webcef_bridge (a C ABI shared library) and cyui_webcef_helper for optional Python/foreign hosts. A host already running CEF should use its own process/app integration rather than initialize a second runtime.

Native lifecycle#

  1. Pass cyui::webCEFApp() to both CefExecuteProcess and CefInitialize before creating views. Use the same renderer handler in all helper executables.
  2. Set CefSettings.windowless_rendering_enabled = true. The application owns CEF initialization, sandbox policy, cache/profile directory and subprocess paths.
  3. Supply an upload callback accepting an upper-left-origin BGRA8 buffer. Update a reusable host GPU texture and return its ImTextureID. The buffer expires after the callback. The texture remains host-owned. The optional release callback runs once, when the browser has closed, with the last texture returned by upload: the view no longer draws it. Free it only once no submitted frame references it (renderers with frames in flight defer by that many frames).
  4. Call CefDoMessageLoopWork() once per loop iteration outside the ImGui frame (before NewFrame, never between NewFrame and Render). upload and release run inside it, so texture updates and releases never race a draw list that is being built. Then NewFrame, beginFrame(), webPanel, endFrame(), Render. The end call hides an undrawn tab/panel.
  5. Call close() on all views and keep pumping until closed(). Destroy views before GPU resources, then call CefShutdown() on the initializing thread.

Every backend call must run on the CEF UI thread (the thread that called CefInitialize with the single-threaded loop). Calls from another thread are ignored and return false, construction throws; debug builds also assert.

cpp
#include <cyui/adapters/WebCEF.h> cyui::WebCEFOptions options;options.url = "http://127.0.0.1:4173/chat";options.policy.origins = {"http://127.0.0.1:4173"};options.upload = [&](int width, int height, const void* bgra) {    return renderer.updateBrowserTexture(width, height, bgra);};options.release = [&](ImTextureID texture) { renderer.releaseAfterFramesInFlight(texture); };auto web = cyui::createWebCEF(options); // after CefInitialize // Each host loop iteration, on the same thread:CefDoMessageLoopWork();       // outside the ImGui frameImGui::NewFrame();web->beginFrame();if (ImGui::Begin("Chat")) {    for (const auto& event : cyui::webPanel("##chat", *web, {0, 0})) {        if (event.kind == cyui::WebEventKind::navigated)            web->postJson(cyui::webThemeJson());        // Parse/validate application messages; apply host commands explicitly.    }}ImGui::End();web->endFrame();ImGui::Render();

The default software paint path bounds each view to 4096×4096 pixels and 30 fps; options allow limits up to 8192. HTML select popups are composited into the same texture. webPanel forwards mouse buttons (with the press's click count on release, so dblclick fires), both wheels, Unicode characters and keys: letters, digits, F1-F24, punctuation, keypad, navigation/editing keys and left/right modifiers. On Windows the adapter adds the active layout's scan code, so the page receives KeyboardEvent.code. While the panel is focused it owns those keys (ImGui key ownership): Tab, arrows, Space, Enter or Escape do not also move ImGui keyboard navigation or activate other widgets. WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot: focus is taken when it changes from false to true, so a click elsewhere can still unfocus the page. The host must keep platform text input enabled while the backend is focused. Use webCEFBrowser() for platform-native key events, IME composition/candidate placement, accessibility, external file drag/drop or other advanced CEF integrations. These platform features are host responsibilities, not validated by the basic pointer/text/message tests.

CEF message pumping is intentionally single-threaded here. Do not enable CEF's multi-threaded message loop and then invoke this backend from a different ImGui thread. Background engine work stays in CEF's subprocesses.

Browser boundary#

WebPolicy accepts exact HTTP(S) origins, including ports. It rejects credentials, file/javascript URLs, wildcard matching, malformed ports and ambiguous backslashes. Use a loopback server for a built local frontend or an explicitly permitted HTTPS origin. CyUI does not start the frontend's server, compile TypeScript or choose its authentication. CEF retains normal browser networking for page subresources.

Main-frame navigation outside allowed origins and new-window requests (popups, target=_blank) are never opened by the adapter; they become external events. An external event is a request from page content, not a command:

  • Only schemes in WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http, https) are reported; others (file:, ms-settings:, custom protocol handlers...) are dropped. Add a scheme only deliberately.
  • Popups from sub-frames (including cross-origin iframes) are dropped unless they come from a user gesture. Events carry userGesture, mainFrame and the requesting frame's sourceOrigin.
  • Before handing a URL to ShellExecute, open or a system browser, check it against your own scheme/host allow-list and ask the user to confirm. Never pass an event URL to the shell unchecked.

Messages are accepted only from the main frame of an allowed origin and are size checked before parsing. The page-side limit in the renderer follows maxMessageBytes (default 1 MiB, at most 64 MiB). Host messages (postJson) are bound to the origin loaded when they were sent: the renderer drops them if the page has navigated to another origin meanwhile. The event queue holds maxQueuedEvents (256); error/console events have a separate lower cap, maxQueuedErrors (16), so a noisy page cannot evict messages. Anything discarded (full queue, caps, oversized data, refused schemes or popups) is counted and reported by a dropped event whose data is the count. Downloads, media permissions and other permission prompts are denied by the supplied minimal adapter; enable product-specific capabilities in an explicitly reviewed host integration if required.

Process sandbox#

The supplied binaries run CEF without its process sandbox on Windows. Windows sandboxing needs sandbox information created by the executable's entry point; the cyui_webcef_bridge library and the generic cyui_webcef_helper pass none, so the bridge sets no_sandbox = true explicitly. A sandbox request (Python no_sandbox=False, the default) is reported, not honoured: cyui_cef_sandboxed() returns 0, cyui_cef_error() explains it, and CEFRuntime issues a RuntimeWarning and sets sandboxed = False. On Linux the request is passed to Chromium (which needs chrome-sandbox or user namespaces); on macOS the helper bundle must also initialize CefScopedSandboxContext. Neither is validated here.

To sandbox a Windows host with the tested CEF 150 SDK, use CEF's bootstrap layout (see the SDK's cef_sandbox_win.h and CEF's sandbox guide): ship bootstrap.exe (or bootstrapc.exe for console apps) renamed to your application, build the application and its subprocess entry as a DLL exporting RunWinMain / RunConsoleMain, and pass the sandbox_info it receives to both CefExecuteProcess and CefInitialize, with no_sandbox = false. Older SDKs that ship cef_sandbox.lib instead link it into the executable and create CefScopedSandboxInfo in wWinMain. The browser and every helper must use the same arrangement. Validate it on the target system before claiming sandboxing.

Browser JavaScript / TypeScript#

web/ is the MIT @cyui/web package with JavaScript, TypeScript declarations and an optional CSS stylesheet. CEF installs a narrow window.cyuiNative message transport. No Electron or Node API is exposed to the page.

ts
import {createCyUIBridge} from '@cyui/web';const bridge = createCyUIBridge();bridge.on('host.reply', payload => updateView(payload));bridge.send('chat.message', {text: 'Hello'});// Dispose listeners when the embedded UI is destroyed.bridge.close();

Messages contain {protocol: 'cyui.web', version: 1, type, payload, requestId?}. The application owns message schema, authorization and effects. A theme message from webThemeJson()/theme_message() supplies palette CSS variables such as --cyui-bg0, --cyui-text and --cyui-accent; send it again after a theme change. JSON is transported as data through CEF process messages, without interpolating host text as executable JavaScript.

Embedded web frontends#

mountCyMD() supports the existing version-1 iframe protocol: explicit parent origin, frame identity and session checks, ready/open/save/state messages, Blob documents and save acknowledgments. The host supplies onSave; CyUI does not write files. Native JSON does not transport Blob objects: handle document transfer in the host page, with a bounded host protocol when required. Web frontends retain their own services, licenses and adapters. Replace Electron preload/IPC dependencies with explicit host messages where needed.

Python#

python
from cyui_modules.cef import CEFRuntimefrom cyui_modules.web import web_panel, theme_message with CEFRuntime(library_path, helper_path, absolute_cache_path, no_sandbox=True) as runtime:    view = runtime.create(url, (allowed_origin,), upload_bgra_to_host_texture,                          release=release_texture_later)    # Each loop iteration:    runtime.pump()            # before new_frame: uploads/releases happen here    imgui.new_frame()    runtime.begin_frame()    events = web_panel('chat', view, (0, 400))    for event in events:        if event['kind'] == 'navigated':            view.post_json(theme_message())    runtime.end_frame()    imgui.render()

All runtime/view calls must run on the owning UI thread. begin_frame() does not pump; call pump() outside the ImGui frame. The context manager closes and pumps all views before shutting CEF down; shutdown fails while a view is alive, and CEF cannot be initialized again in the same process. An upload callback receives a native pointer valid only during the call; copy/update immediately. release runs from pump() after the view closed. no_sandbox=True states what the bridge does on Windows anyway (see Process sandbox); leaving the default warns. Python's garbage collector does not initialize or shut down a browser on an arbitrary thread.

Deployment and checks#

Native webThemeJson() and Python theme_message() also carry the current UI locale (English by default). Send a fresh theme after changing languages. The JavaScript bridge translates only marked interface elements and exposes a catalog for TypeScript components; see LOCALIZATION.md. Bundle the bridge's cyui-i18n.js and cyui-locales.js imports with the main bridge module.

  • Windows: ship matching libcef/Chromium runtime files, resources/locales, helper executable and supported sandbox setup. The optional test/demo CMake staging copies the selected SDK's Release/Resources into the build output.
  • Linux: ship/use matching libcef.so, resources/locales and helper; configure the runtime search path, target display stack and Chromium sandbox as CEF requires.
  • macOS: package/load Chromium Embedded Framework.framework and correctly named signed helper app bundles, integrate CEF's AppKit application handling, entitlements and sandbox setup. The generic helper source is not a complete macOS app bundle.
  • Keep the selected SDK's LICENSE.txt, CREDITS.html and other component notices. See LICENSING.md.

Calls from another thread are ignored and return false, construction throws; debug builds also assert. cpp Copy # include <cyui/adapters/WebCEF.h> cyui :: WebCEFOptions options ; options . url = "http://127.0.0.1:4173/chat" ; options . policy . origins = { "http://127.0.0.1:4173" } ; options . upload = [ & ] ( int width , int height , const void * bgra ) { return renderer . updateBrowserTexture ( width , height , bgra ) ; } ; options . release = [ & ] ( ImTextureID texture ) { renderer . releaseAfterFramesInFlight ( texture ) ; } ; auto web = cyui :: createWebCEF ( options ) ; // after CefInitialize // Each host loop iteration, on the same thread: CefDoMessageLoopWork ( ) ; // outside the ImGui frame ImGui :: NewFrame ( ) ; web -> beginFrame ( ) ; if ( ImGui :: Begin ( "Chat" ) ) { for ( const auto & event : cyui :: webPanel ( "##chat" , * web , { 0 , 0 } ) ) { if ( event . kind == cyui :: WebEventKind :: navigated ) web -> postJson ( cyui :: webThemeJson ( ) ) ; // Parse/validate application messages; apply host commands explicitly. } } ImGui :: End ( ) ; web -> endFrame ( ) ; ImGui :: Render ( ) ; The default software paint path bounds each view to 4096×4096 pixels and 30 fps; options allow limits up to 8192. HTML select popups are composited into the same texture. webPanel forwards mouse buttons (with the press's click count on release, so dblclick fires), both wheels, Unicode characters and keys: letters, digits, F1-F24, punctuation, keypad, navigation/editing keys and left/right modifiers. On Windows the adapter adds the active layout's scan code, so the page receives KeyboardEvent.code . While the panel is focused it owns those keys (ImGui key ownership): Tab, arrows, Space, Enter or Escape do not also move ImGui keyboard navigation or activate other widgets. WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot: focus is taken when it changes from false to true, so a click elsewhere can still unfocus the page. The host must keep platform text input enabled while the backend is focused. Use webCEFBrowser() for platform-native key events, IME composition/candidate placement, accessibility, external file drag/drop or other advanced CEF integrations. These platform features are host responsibilities, not validated by the basic pointer/text/message tests. CEF message pumping is intentionally single-threaded here. Do not enable CEF's multi-threaded message loop and then invoke this backend from a different ImGui thread. Background engine work stays in CEF's subprocesses. Browser boundary # WebPolicy accepts exact HTTP(S) origins, including ports. It rejects credentials, file/javascript URLs, wildcard matching, malformed ports and ambiguous backslashes. Use a loopback server for a built local frontend or an explicitly permitted HTTPS origin. CyUI does not start the frontend's server, compile TypeScript or choose its authentication. CEF retains normal browser networking for page subresources. Main-frame navigation outside allowed origins and new-window requests (popups, target=_blank ) are never opened by the adapter; they become external events. An external event is a request from page content, not a command: Only schemes in WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http , https ) are reported; others ( file: , ms-settings: , custom protocol handlers...) are dropped. Add a scheme only deliberately. Popups from sub-frames (including cross-origin iframes) are dropped unless they come from a user gesture. Events carry userGesture , mainFrame and the requesting frame's sourceOrigin . Before handing a URL to ShellExecute , open or a system browser, check it against your own scheme/host allow-list and ask the user to confirm. Never pass an event URL to the shell unchecked. Messages are accepted only from the main frame of an allowed origin and are size checked before parsing. The page-side limit in the renderer follows maxMessageBytes (default 1 MiB, at most 64 MiB). Host messages ( postJson ) are bound to the origin loaded when they were sent: the renderer drops them if the page has navigated to another origin meanwhile. The event queue holds maxQueuedEvents (256); error/console events have a separate lower cap, maxQueuedErrors (16), so a noisy page cannot evict messages. Anything discarded (full queue, caps, oversized data, refused schemes or popups) is counted and reported by a dropped event whose data is the count. Downloads, media permissions and other permission prompts are denied by the supplied minimal adapter; enable product-specific capabilities in an explicitly reviewed host integration if required. Process sandbox # The supplied binaries run CEF without its process sandbox on Windows. Windows sandboxing needs sandbox information created by the executable's entry point; the cyui_webcef_bridge library and the generic cyui_webcef_helper pass none, so the bridge sets no_sandbox = true explicitly. A sandbox request (Python no_sandbox=False , the default) is reported, not honoured: cyui_cef_sandboxed() returns 0, cyui_cef_error() explains it, and CEFRuntime issues a RuntimeWarning and sets sandboxed = False . On Linux the request is passed to Chromium (which needs chrome-sandbox or user namespaces); on macOS the helper bundle must also initialize CefScopedSandboxContext . Neither is validated here. To sandbox a Windows host with the tested CEF 150 SDK, use CEF's bootstrap layout (see the SDK's cef_sandbox_win.h and CEF's sandbox guide): ship bootstrap.exe (or bootstrapc.exe for console apps) renamed to your application, build the application and its subprocess entry as a DLL exporting RunWinMain / RunConsoleMain , and pass the sandbox_info it receives to both CefExecuteProcess and CefInitialize , with no_sandbox = false . Older SDKs that ship cef_sandbox.lib instead link it into the executable and create CefScopedSandboxInfo in wWinMain . The browser and every helper must use the same arrangement. Validate it on the target system before claiming sandboxing. Browser JavaScript / TypeScript # web/ is the MIT @cyui/web package with JavaScript, TypeScript declarations and an optional CSS stylesheet. CEF installs a narrow window.cyuiNative message transport. No Electron or Node API is exposed to the page. ts Copy import { createCyUIBridge } from '@cyui/web' ; const bridge = createCyUIBridge ( ) ; bridge . on ( 'host.reply' , payload => updateView ( payload ) ) ; bridge . send ( 'chat.message' , { text : 'Hello' } ) ; // Dispose listeners when the embedded UI is destroyed. bridge . close ( ) ; Messages contain {protocol: 'cyui.web', version: 1, type, payload, requestId?} . The application owns message schema, authorization and effects. A theme message from webThemeJson()/theme_message() supplies palette CSS variables such as --cyui-bg0 , --cyui-text and --cyui-accent ; send it again after a theme change. JSON is transported as data through CEF process messages, without interpolating host text as executable JavaScript. Embedded web frontends # mountCyMD() supports the existing version-1 iframe protocol: explicit parent origin, frame identity and session checks, ready/open/save/state messages, Blob documents and save acknowledgments. The host supplies onSave; CyUI does not write files. Native JSON does not transport Blob objects: handle document transfer in the host page, with a bounded host protocol when required. Web frontends retain their own services, licenses and adapters. Replace Electron preload/IPC dependencies with explicit host messages where needed. Python # python Copy from cyui_modules . cef import CEFRuntime from cyui_modules . web import web_panel , theme_message with CEFRuntime ( library_path , helper_path , absolute_cache_path , no_sandbox = True ) as runtime : view = runtime . create ( url , ( allowed_origin , ) , upload_bgra_to_host_texture , release = release_texture_later ) # Each loop iteration: runtime . pump ( ) # before new_frame: uploads/releases happen here imgui . new_frame ( ) runtime . begin_frame ( ) events = web_panel ( 'chat' , view , ( 0 , 400 ) ) for event in events : if event [ 'kind' ] == 'navigated' : view . post_json ( theme_message ( ) ) runtime . end_frame ( ) imgui . render ( ) All runtime/view calls must run on the owning UI thread. begin_frame() does not pump; call pump() outside the ImGui frame. The context manager closes and pumps all views before shutting CEF down; shutdown fails while a view is alive, and CEF cannot be initialized again in the same process. An upload callback receives a native pointer valid only during the call; copy/update immediately. release runs from pump() after the view closed. no_sandbox=True states what the bridge does on Windows anyway (see Process sandbox); leaving the default warns. Python's garbage collector does not initialize or shut down a browser on an arbitrary thread. Deployment and checks # Native webThemeJson() and Python theme_message() also carry the current UI locale (English by default). Send a fresh theme after changing languages. The JavaScript bridge translates only marked interface elements and exposes a catalog for TypeScript components; see LOCALIZATION.md . Bundle the bridge's cyui-i18n.js and cyui-locales.js imports with the main bridge module. Windows: ship matching libcef/Chromium runtime files, resources/locales, helper executable and supported sandbox setup. The optional test/demo CMake staging copies the selected SDK's Release/Resources into the build output. Linux: ship/use matching libcef.so, resources/locales and helper; configure the runtime search path, target display stack and Chromium sandbox as CEF requires. macOS: package/load Chromium Embedded Framework.framework and correctly named signed helper app bundles, integrate CEF's AppKit application handling, entitlements and sandbox setup. The generic helper source is not a complete macOS app bundle. Keep the selected SDK's LICENSE.txt, CREDITS.html and other component notices. See LICENSING.md . set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_MODULES "Web" CACHE STRING "" FORCE) set(CYUI_BUILD_WEB_CEF ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_CEF_ROOT "path/to/extracted/cef_binary_distribution" CACHE PATH "" FORCE) add_subdirectory(external/CyUI) target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::WebCEF) #include <cyui/adapters/WebCEF.h> cyui::WebCEFOptions options; options.url = "http://127.0.0.1:4173/chat"; options.policy.origins = {"http://127.0.0.1:4173"}; options.upload = [&](int width, int height, const void* bgra) { return renderer.updateBrowserTexture(width, height, bgra); }; options.release = [&](ImTextureID texture) { renderer.releaseAfterFramesInFlight(texture); }; auto web = cyui::createWebCEF(options); // after CefInitialize // Each host loop iteration, on the same thread: CefDoMessageLoopWork(); // outside the ImGui frame ImGui::NewFrame(); web->beginFrame(); if (ImGui::Begin("Chat")) { for (const auto& event : cyui::webPanel("##chat", *web, {0, 0})) { if (event.kind == cyui::WebEventKind::navigated) web->postJson(cyui::webThemeJson()); // Parse/validate application messages; apply host commands explicitly. } } ImGui::End(); web->endFrame(); ImGui::Render(); import {createCyUIBridge} from '@cyui/web'; const bridge = createCyUIBridge(); bridge.on('host.reply', payload => updateView(payload)); bridge.send('chat.message', {text: 'Hello'}); // Dispose listeners when the embedded UI is destroyed. bridge.close(); from cyui_modules.cef import CEFRuntime from cyui_modules.web import web_panel, theme_message with CEFRuntime(library_path, helper_path, absolute_cache_path, no_sandbox=True) as runtime: view = runtime.create(url, (allowed_origin,), upload_bgra_to_host_texture, release=release_texture_later) # Each loop iteration: runtime.pump() # before new_frame: uploads/releases happen here imgui.new_frame() runtime.begin_frame() events = web_panel('chat', view, (0, 400)) for event in events: if event['kind'] == 'navigated': view.post_json(theme_message()) runtime.end_frame() imgui.render()

pages.title: Widget API reference
pages.description: Widget API reference for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
All functions are in namespace cyui. The headers carry the full comments.

Units. Widget size and width parameters are screen pixels: wrap design values in dp(), as in cyui::button("OK", cyui::dp(80, 0)). 0 means automatic, and a negative width fills the row minus that much. These are design units, scaled inside:

  • beginCard height
  • beginProperties label width
  • beginSidebar and beginModal widths
  • space height, divider spacing, spinner radius
  • KnobStyle::diameter

beginTopBar's height is in pixels.

Disabled and edited. Inside ScopedDisabled, CyUI's hand-drawn widgets fade and stop reacting, like stock ImGui. Every CyUI control that changes a value marks it edited, so ImGui::IsItemEdited() is true after it on that frame. Clicks and drags also give ImGui::IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit() on release: one undo step per gesture. Wheel nudges and typed values are one-shot edits that only set IsItemEdited(). markEdited(id) does the same for your own controls.

Theme (Theme.h)#

  • Setup: apply(Config), applyDpi(s), dpi() (the current scale), loadFonts(FontConfig).
  • Palette: palette(), setPalette(p), setTheme("key"), builtInThemes(), currentThemeKey(). paletteFields() lists each role with its key, label, group and member pointer, for editors and theme files.
  • Density and metrics: setDensity(d), density(), metrics(). The metrics give the font size, paddings, roundings, cardPadding and toolbarHeight.
  • Fonts: uiFont(), boldFont(), monoFont(), iconsAvailable(). The fonts are null until loadFonts filled the context's atlas. ScopedFont(nullptr, factor) then keeps the current font.
  • Colour helpers: rgb(0xRRGGBB, a), alpha, mix, brighter, darker, vec, categorical(i). categorical gives 12 hues derived from the palette, toned for light or dark grounds.
  • Sizes: dp(v) / dp(x, y).
  • Theme files: savePalette(path, p), loadPalette(path, p), paletteToText, paletteFromText. The .cytheme format is key = #RRGGBB[AA]; CyDAW's JSON .cytheme files also load.

Icons (Icons.h)#

cyui::icon::play, pause, stop, record, add, remove, trash, settings, search, folder, save, undo, redo, edit, close, check, chevronDown, more, refresh, zoomIn, lock, filter, loop, library, star, copy, paste, info, warning, home, globe, people, mail, calendar, clock, cloud, upload, download, code, photo, document, ... (104 icons). They are UTF-8 strings of Segoe MDL2 Assets, so they work in any label: std::string(icon::save) + " Save". They draw only on Windows. Without the icon font, the CyUI widgets fall back:

  • iconButton shows the first letter of its tooltip when the current font lacks the glyph (a host's own merged icon font still works).
  • iconTextButton shows the label alone.
  • sidebarItem and emptyState leave the icon out.
  • helpMarker shows (?).

Guard your own icon labels with iconsAvailable().

Text (CoreWidgets.h)#

  • heading(t, level), sectionTitle(t), overline(T)
  • textDim(fmt, ...), textFaint(fmt, ...), textColoured(c, fmt, ...), textMono(fmt, ...)
  • kbd("Ctrl+S"), helpMarker(t), tooltip(t)
  • clippedText(list, pos, w, c, t), centredText(list, min, max, c, t)

Buttons#

  • toneColour(Tone): the palette colour of a tone (neutral is textDim).
  • button(label, Variant, size). The variants are secondary, primary, ghost, outline, danger and success.
  • Shortcuts: primaryButton, dangerButton, ghostButton.
  • iconTextButton(icon, label, variant)
  • iconButton(icon, tooltip, active, activeColour, size)
  • toggleButton(label, &b, onColour, size, tooltip): compact pills such as M, S and R.
  • toggleSwitch(label, &b)
  • segmented(id, labels, n, &current, width). A width of -1 fills the row.
  • linkText(label)

Values#

  • knob(id, &v, min, max, default, KnobStyle{diameter, colour, label, format, unit}). Set KnobStyle.flags to knobBipolar, knobLogarithmic, knobInteger or knobNoLabel. .steps and .modulation are also available.
  • fader(id, &dB, minDb, maxDb, size, colour)
  • meter(id, size, peakL, peakR, rmsL, rmsR, vertical)
  • dragValue(id, &v, speed, min, max, fmt, width). speed is per pixel dragged. Once the field has the focus (clicked or navigated to), a wheel notch moves 10 × speed; before that, the wheel scrolls the panel. min >= max is unbounded.
  • sliderBar(id, &v, min, max, fmt, width, colour). A click or a drag sets the value. A wheel notch moves 1 % of the range.
  • valueEntry(...): the typed number field these controls open. valueEntryOpen() says whether one is open (to hold back shortcuts while the user types).
  • itemWheel(): the wheel for your own control, claimed in time so the panel under it does not scroll. Also takeWheel(), wheelTaken() and valueSpeed().

The value controls share these interactions:

  • drag to change; Ctrl is fine (× 0.15), Shift is fast (× 4)
  • the mouse wheel nudges the value and does not scroll the panel under it (a dragValue only once it has the focus)
  • a double click types the value (dragValue, sliderBar) or resets it (a knob)
  • a click on a knob's value types it

Fields#

  • searchField(id, buf, size, hint, width)
  • textField(id, buf, size, hint, width)
  • combo(id, &i, items, n, width)

Quick filtering (Filter.h, included in Core)#

Provide a quick filter in menus and panels where users need to find actions or properties. Keep a TextFilter in each view's state. filterBox(id, state) draws the query field; panelHeader(title, subtitle, &state) includes it in the heading. Use state.matches(englishLabel, keywordsAndSectionPath) before drawing a row. Search uses all words, ignoring ASCII/Latin case and accents, and checks both the English key and the current translation. Hidden ImGui IDs are excluded.

beginFilteredSection(label, state, hasMatchingChildren, defaultOpen) reveals a matching section without changing its saved collapse preference; pair with endSection() when true. filterMenu(id, state, entries) draws a searchable menu inside an already open ImGui menu/popup. Its FilterMenuItem tree retains action IDs, disabled/checked states and shortcuts. Searching lists matching descendants with breadcrumbs. The host handles the returned action ID.

InspectorOptions{&state, sectionTitle} enables filtering in inspector(); propertyMatches(state, property, sectionTitle) helps choose visible sections. Call Inspector for a section's full property model so hidden active edits can be cancelled; when omitting an entire panel, cancel its host previews explicitly. Read FILTERING.md for complete C++ and Python examples and limits. These helpers do not intercept raw ImGui calls or patch Dear ImGui.

Containers#

  • beginCard(id, title, height, tone) / endCard(). Always call endCard, whatever beginCard returned.
  • beginSection(label, defaultOpen) / endSection(). Call endSection only when beginSection returned true.
  • beginProperties(id, labelWidth) / property(label, help) / endProperties(). Call endProperties only when beginProperties returned true. property() sets up full width for the next widget.
  • toolbarSeparator(), divider(spacing), space(h)

Status#

  • badge(t, Tone), statusDot(c, tip)
  • progressBar(f, size, overlay, Tone). A fraction f < 0 gives an indeterminate bar.
  • spinner(id, r, c)
  • emptyState(title, msg, icon)
  • callout(Tone, text)
  • colourChip(id, c, size)
  • notify(text, Tone, seconds) shows a toast in the current ImGui context. With no context current, it goes to the one context CyUI knows. When there are several or none, it asserts in debug builds and drops the toast. notify(context, text, Tone, seconds) posts to a given context, from any thread. Call renderNotifications() once per frame. At most six toasts show at a time.

Layout (Layout.h)#

The application shell. Call these in the frame in this order: menu bar, top bar, status bar, sidebar, then dock space.

  • beginTopBar(id, h) / endTopBar()
  • beginStatusBar(id) / endStatusBar(), with statusText(Tone, fmt, ...)
  • beginSidebar(id, w) / endSidebar(), with sidebarHeader(title, badge), sidebarGroup(LABEL) and sidebarItem(icon, label, active, badge)
  • dockSpace(id, flags) (docking branch)
  • panelHeader(title, subtitle)
  • panelHeader(title, subtitle, &filter) to add a quick filter
  • beginToolbar(id) / endToolbar()
  • beginModal(title, &open, width) / endModal(). Call endModal only when beginModal returned true. modalButtons(confirm, cancel, danger) returns 1 for confirm and 2 for cancel. Enter confirms and Escape cancels. Modals can nest: each modalButtons closes its own modal.
  • alignRight(width), buttonWidth(label)

All begin*Bar / beginSidebar / beginToolbar must be paired with their end*, whatever they returned. Popups and tooltips opened from a bar keep the theme's style.

Gallery (Gallery.h)#

  • showGallery(&open, selectTab): every widget, a theme switcher and a density switcher. selectTab brings a page to the front once:
    • 0 text, 1 buttons, 2 controls, 3 containers
    • 4–19 the optional modules
    • 20 layout (the application shell), 21 filtering (menus and panels)
  • showGallery(&open, selectTab, GalleryResources): the same, with host resources for the module pages: texture, width and height (Images, Viewport), web (a live Web backend) and previewCommands.
  • showThemeEditor(&open): live palette editing and .cytheme save and load.

GalleryResources::openDocumentation(page, section) optionally routes the Filtering example’s Help action to the host’s local reader at filtering/searchable-menus. Keep its callback owner alive during drawing. Gallery does not launch a browser itself.

Call endModal only when beginModal returned true. modalButtons(confirm, cancel, danger) returns 1 for confirm and 2 for cancel. Enter confirms and Escape cancels. Modals can nest: each modalButtons closes its own modal. alignRight(width) , buttonWidth(label) All begin*Bar / beginSidebar / beginToolbar must be paired with their end* , whatever they returned. Popups and tooltips opened from a bar keep the theme's style. Gallery ( Gallery.h ) # showGallery(&open, selectTab) : every widget, a theme switcher and a density switcher. selectTab brings a page to the front once: 0 text, 1 buttons, 2 controls, 3 containers 4–19 the optional modules 20 layout (the application shell), 21 filtering (menus and panels) showGallery(&open, selectTab, GalleryResources) : the same, with host resources for the module pages: texture , width and height (Images, Viewport), web (a live Web backend) and previewCommands . showThemeEditor(&open) : live palette editing and .cytheme save and load. GalleryResources::openDocumentation(page, section) optionally routes the Filtering example’s Help action to the host’s local reader at filtering/searchable-menus . Keep its callback owner alive during drawing. Gallery does not launch a browser itself.

pages.title: Syntaxe C++ et extensions
pages.description: Utiliser les 102 modes natifs et enregistrer une syntaxe applicative.
pages.html:
Liez CyUI::Code (C++17) pour le catalogue, les lexers et les vues en lecture seule ; CyUI::CodeEditor (C++20) ajoute l’édition. Core seul ne compile ni ne lie de lexer. CMake résout les dépendances et exporte CYUI_CODE_LANGUAGE_CATALOGUE=1. Le catalogue commité se compile sans réseau ni Python, avec une seule instance compatible d’ImGui.

Modes intégrés#

codeLanguages() retourne 102 instantanés de métadonnées possédées. data/code-languages.json définit la liste canonique, les associations et les profils de shaders. Le catalogue couvre les modes de syntaxe de Notepad++ utilisés pour l’intégration, plus HLSL, GLSL, Markdown, TSX et un profil Unreal C++. Chaque mode possède un exemple. NFO s’affiche volontairement en texte brut : le décodage OEM relève de l’hôte. Internal Search colore une liste de diagnostics, sans moteur de recherche. Aucun composant UI, ABI de plugin ou format de configuration Notepad++ n’est inclus.

codeLanguageFromName(idOrName) accepte IDs, noms et quelques alias, puis retombe sur plain. codeLanguageForPath(path) teste les noms exacts puis les extensions sans tenir compte de la casse. Ajoutez un contexte de projet pour les cas ambigus comme les en-têtes Unreal, ou un choix manuel. Les associations de plugins ont priorité ; leur retrait restaure les modes intégrés. Les conflits entre plugins sont déterministes par ID numérique stable.

Ajouter une syntaxe depuis un plugin#

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/Code.h>cyui::CodeLanguageDefinition syntax;syntax.id = "my-plugin/config";  // stable, namespaced IDsyntax.name = "My configuration";syntax.extensions = {"mycfg"}; // no leading dotcyui::CodeSyntaxRules rules;rules.keywords = {"option", "section"};rules.types = {"number", "vector"};rules.lineComment = "#";rules.blockCommentStart = "/*";rules.blockCommentEnd = "*/";syntax.rules = rules;const auto language = cyui::registerCodeLanguage(syntax);// view.setText(source, language, documentRevision);// editor.setLanguage(language);// On plugin removal, after stopping calls and before unloading its code:cyui::unregisterCodeLanguage(syntax.id);

Vous pouvez aussi définir base sur un mode intégré, ses wordLists Lexilla numérotées depuis zéro et des properties. Les listes vides héritent de la base. Les règles acceptent un délimiteur de commentaire de ligne, une paire de bloc, des guillemets, échappements et ensembles de mots sensibles ou non à la casse. Pour une grammaire imbriquée ou un parseur spécifique, fournissez highlight(std::string_view) -> std::vector<CodeToken>. La priorité est callback, règles, puis moteur de base.

Les tokens utilisent des offsets en octets UTF-8 bruts, pas des colonnes visuelles, positions UTF-16 ou tabulations développées. Les plages sont non vides, triées, disjointes, bornées par l’instantané et les limites de points de code. Les espaces non couverts restent neutres. Rôles inconnus et plages invalides déclenchent une exception avant remplacement du document préparé. Les thèmes donnent les couleurs par rôle ; aucun littéral de couleur UI n’est fourni par le plugin. Les définitions et instantanés sont bornés (source : 32 Mio). L’hôte traite les erreurs et limites de temps de son code de plugin.

Réenregistrer un ID de plugin le met à jour sans changer sa valeur numérique. Les valeurs intégrées 0..13 sont conservées ; les valeurs dynamiques utilisent le bit fort. Persistez l’ID texte, pas le numéro dynamique. Les modes intégrés ne peuvent pas être remplacés ; les collisions de hachage sont refusées. Les instantanés du registre sont synchronisés, mais les callbacks s’exécutent hors mutex. Leur durée de vie appartient à l’hôte : le retrait n’attend pas les appels déjà en cours. Arrêtez et joignez ces appels avant de décharger la bibliothèque ou ses services capturés.

Cache, édition et limites#

CodeDocument met en cache révisions du document et du registre. CodeEditor ne recolore qu’après un changement de texte natif ou de registre. Lexilla relit l’instantané borné entier après une édition : ce n’est pas un parseur incrémental. Une modification pendant le dessin reçoit les nouvelles couleurs à la frame suivante. refreshSyntax() prépare explicitement, même sans fenêtre. La préparation ne modifie ni octets, ni curseur, ni historique Undo. setSyntaxEnabled(false) conserve les adaptateurs lexicaux/sémantiques d’un hôte plus riche sans imposer un autre éditeur.

Il s’agit de coloration lexicale, sans complétion LSP, refactoring ou sémantique de compilateur. Les modules Python historiques gardent leur implémentation ; cette nouvelle API native de registre et callbacks est C++ et ne fournit pas de liaison Python.

Dépendances embarquées#

third_party/code-syntax.lock.json fige les révisions Lexilla, en-têtes Scintilla, propriétés SciTE et les sommes des archives. Seuls les moteurs Lexilla sélectionnés et leur bibliothèque de support sont compilés, sans l’éditeur Scintilla. Conservez les trois licences et THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Fichiers de journal#

CodeLanguage::log reconnaît .log/.logs et colore la ligne entière. INFO et les lignes non marquées gardent le texte normal.

Mot de niveau, sans sensibilité à la casse Rôle
Error, Fatal, Critical, Panic, Exception error, rouge par défaut
Warning, Warn warning, orange
Debug, Trace, Verbose, VeryVerbose comment, atténué
Autres, y compris Info text, normal

Seuls les mots complets comptent : ErrorCode, WarningCount et traceback ne sont pas des niveaux. Priorité à l’erreur, puis avertissement, puis verbosité. Les niveaux entre crochets, LogTemp: Error:, champs JSON et préfixes horodatés sont pris en compte. Les séquences ANSI CSI sont ignorées pour la détection mais les octets restent intacts. Les lignes visuelles repliées héritent de la couleur. Les continuations de pile sans niveau restent normales ; l’hôte gère les événements multilignes et l’élimination des échappements. Un plugin peut hériter de CodeLanguage::log ou fournir son callback.

Verse#

CodeLanguage::verse / verse sélectionne le scanner natif original. .verse est reconnu sans tenir compte de la casse, y compris *.digest.verse. Aucun SDK UEFN, moteur Lexilla supplémentaire ou serveur de langage n’est lié. CodeEditor et CodeDocument partagent les tokens : mots-clés, types, effets/spécificateurs d’accès, attributs, appels, nombres décimaux/hexadécimaux/exponentiels, chaînes et caractères ont des rôles sémantiques.

Les commentaires #, blocs imbriqués <# ... #> et commentaires indentés <#> gardent leur état entre lignes. L’interpolation des chaînes colore les expressions, accolades imbriquées, chaînes et commentaires ; les accolades échappées restent du texte. Une chaîne ou un commentaire inachevé garde sa couleur jusqu’à la fin. L’imbrication est bornée à 63 niveaux ; au-delà, le reste est affiché comme chaîne. Les octets et Undo ne changent pas.

Un plugin peut hériter de base = CodeLanguage::verse ; les ensembles 0/1/2 remplacent mots-clés, types et fonctions, les entrées vides héritent des valeurs par défaut. Règles et callbacks restent prioritaires, et le retrait restaure les associations. La coloration ne fournit ni compilation Verse, ni complétion UEFN, ni analyse sémantique.

Références : Book of Verse et référence Epic.

pages.title: Thèmes, disposition et migration
pages.description: Appliquer les rôles de palette, les dimensions DPI et les composants adaptés.
pages.html:
Choisissez chaque couleur dans cyui::palette() et chaque dimension dans cyui::dp() ou le style. Une interface cohérente utilise les mêmes règles dans les widgets standards et les dessins personnalisés.

Rôle Usage
bg0 Fond profond des canevas, timelines et barres d’état
bg1 Fond des panneaux
bg2 En-têtes, cartes et fenêtres contextuelles
bg3, bg4, bg5 Contrôle au repos, survolé, pressé/actif
line, lineStrong Traits et séparateurs
text, textDim, textFaint Texte principal, secondaire et indications
accent, accentHover, accentDim, accentText, selection Action principale, activité et sélection
success, warning, error, info Couleurs sémantiques

Utilisez alpha, mix, brighter et darker pour les variantes, categorical(i) pour les séries. Gardez un accent principal et un rendu plat. Pour les tailles, préférez aussi GetFrameHeight, GetFontSize et GetStyle.

Les titres utilisent heading(texte, 1|2|3), les groupes sectionTitle, les petites étiquettes overline. textDim et textFaint créent les niveaux secondaires. Évitez de fabriquer un titre avec Text et une couleur poussée.

Une vue possède une action principale (primaryButton) ; utilisez button pour les autres actions, ghostButton/iconButton dans les barres d’outils et dangerButton pour les suppressions. Chaque bouton d’icône doit avoir une infobulle indiquant son action et son raccourci. Séparez les groupes par toolbarSeparator.

Présentez les réglages dans beginProperties/property/endProperties, au sein de sections repliables. Groupez les contenus dans des cartes ; réservez les tons accent/avertissement/erreur aux situations qui demandent de l’attention. Un panneau vide explique l’action possible avec emptyState.

Signalez les événements avec notify, les conditions persistantes avec callout, les tâches avec progressBar ou spinner et les états avec badge ou statusDot. Les infobulles tooltip sont retardées et reviennent à la ligne ; helpMarker explique une option.

Conservez les contrôles ImGui standards lisibles : Checkbox, InputText, ColorEdit, tableaux, arbres, menus, onglets et DragFloat2 reçoivent le thème. Préférez ScopedColor, ScopedVar, ScopedFont, ScopedID et ScopedDisabled aux piles Push/Pop manuelles. N’appelez pas StyleColors* après apply ; changez la palette avec setPalette. Utilisez ScopedFont plutôt que SetWindowFontScale, et une identité stable Label###stableId pour un libellé variable.

Migrer une interface ImGui#

Procédez panneau par panneau en conservant les identifiants, la logique et les comportements.

Ancien code Remplacement
Fonction de thème, StyleColorsDark, couleurs de style apply(config) puis loadFonts()
Couleurs IM_COL32 ou ImVec4 du dessin UI Rôle de palette()
Taille fixe en pixels dp(valeur)
Bouton principal / suppression primaryButton / dangerButton
Petit bouton de barre d’outils iconButton(icon, tooltip, selected)
Checkbox de réglage toggleSwitch ; conserver Checkbox dans les listes
Rangée de boutons de mode segmented
Texte de section et séparateur sectionTitle ou beginSection
Texte gris personnalisé textDim / textFaint
Label, SameLine puis champ Table beginProperties et property
Curseur dans un inspecteur sliderBar, ou conserver SliderFloat
Champ de recherche searchField
BeginChild utilisé comme carte beginCard/endCard
Barre de progression progressBar
Confirmation modale beginModal/modalButtons
Message d’état ponctuel notify
Barres de fenêtre positionnées manuellement beginTopBar, beginStatusBar, beginSidebar
Contrôles audio dessinés à la main knob, fader, meter du module Audio

Les vues personnalisées peuvent conserver leurs dessins : fond bg0, grille grid/gridStrong, sélection selection bordée d’accent, texte text/textDim, poignées bg5 ou accent. Ouvrez showGallery() depuis un menu de développement et contrôlez les cinq thèmes ainsi que les deux densités pour détecter les contrastes incorrects.

Comparer les thèmes#
